You will own Daybreak’s government product enablement strategy and personally design and deliver the training that brings it to life. Your work will span audience research, curriculum design, recorded demonstrations and courses, hands-on workshops, executive briefings, and cyber councils. You will work directly with U.S. and international government cyber leaders to translate frontier AI capabilities into practical workflows that address operational challenges.
You will also partner with the cyber product team, bringing customer feedback, deployment challenges, and adversarial context into product development. Your work will help shape best practices for adopting and deploying our cyber tools, strengthen government cyber defenses, and inform the direction of these capabilities.
You will engage across the government cybersecurity ecosystem, including Authorizing Officials (AOs), CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior executives. Practitioners need practical proficiency; executives need a strategic understanding of our cyber products, their value, and their implications for mission and risk. Success means demonstrated capability, sustained adoption, and better cyber outcomes.
This role is based in Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL
- Set the vision and own the execution of Daybreak’s government enablement strategy, from audience research and learning objectives to curriculum, delivery, and measurable mission impact.
- Serve as a trusted cyber ambassador for OpenAI, leading substantive conversations about our tools and capabilities with U.S. and international government leaders, customers, and the broader cyber community.
- Help government leaders understand and respond to AI’s changing cyber landscape through executive briefings, public speaking, and thought leadership grounded in operational experience.
- Personally lead technical training, live demonstrations, hands-on workshops, and executive conversations that help AOs, CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior leaders apply Daybreak to their work.
- Bring frontline experience into product development. Serve as a key point of contact for Daybreak Blue and Red, translating user feedback, deployment friction, and unmet mission needs into actionable product recommendations.
- Create practical learning materials, including scripts, recorded demonstrations, interactive labs, digital courses, videos, facilitator guides, and playbooks.
- Convene and lead our cyber councils, bringing leaders and practitioners into candid conversations that surface hard questions, share field lessons, and build a community of practice.
- Deliver tailored engagements for specialist teams and repeatable learning programs that equip thousands of practitioners to use Daybreak effectively.
- Translate frontier capabilities into practical government workflows across the cybersecurity lifecycle, connecting Daybreak’s applications and deployment requirements to challenges such as critical infrastructure security and defense of critical networks.
- Develop practical guidance for human-machine teaming in cyber, including where AI adds value, where human judgment is essential, and how teams validate results and act responsibly.
- Coordinate across product, security, deployment, and customer teams to address adoption barriers and keep enablement technically accurate, operationally relevant, and current as capabilities and requirements evolve.
- Assess demonstrated proficiency, track sustained adoption, and use evidence of stronger cyber performance and mission outcomes to improve programs.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU
- Hold an active security clearance, preferably TS/SCI
- Bring deep cybersecurity expertise across threat modeling, vulnerability discovery and validation, prioritization, remediation, detection, incident response, and recovery, with the judgment to connect these disciplines to government missions.
- Have deep fluency in Daybreak’s capabilities, applications, and deployment requirements, and can translate that knowledge into credible advice and practical government cyber training.
- Have personally built and delivered cybersecurity enablement that changed how people work, from focused engagements with specialist teams to programs reaching thousands of practitioners.
- Are a compelling speaker, writer, educator, and hands-on creator. You can set the strategy, write the script, record the demonstration, build the lab, and lead the workshop, roundtable, or private executive session.
- Can earn trust in executive briefings and technical deep dives, adapting your language, examples, and level of detail while giving audiences a clear reason and a practical way to act.
- Know how to read a leader and a room. You combine presence and emotional intelligence with humility, listen carefully, welcome hard questions, and make people comfortable learning something new.
- Understand government cyber missions, security requirements, and operational constraints, ideally across DOW, federal civilian agencies, and state and local government, and can build approaches that work within those realities.
- Turn ambitious goals into disciplined execution, leading cross-functional work, incorporating feedback, and taking ownership of demonstrated proficiency, sustained product use, and stronger defenses.
- Have built and led teams of cyber enablement professionals, setting a high bar for technical credibility, teaching quality, and execution while helping others grow.
- Bring a practical understanding of U.S. cybersecurity laws, regulations, and policies, and can explain their implications for government adoption and deployment.
- Have served in a government cyber role and bring a deep commitment to the people behind the mission, including public servants, warfighters, and the intelligence community.

About the Team
The ChatGPT Velocity team owns the health of the end-to-end developer and deploy loop for ChatGPT-facing services. Our mission is to help ChatGPT engineers ship confidently with a fast, lightweight development cycle and a trusted path to production.
ChatGPT development depends on a long chain: local environments, Bazel builds, CI, tests, merges, release candidates, deploys, synthetics, alerts, and production health. When any link is slow, flaky, or unclear, engineers lose hours, fixes reach users later, and on-call load rises. This team turns that cross-cutting drag into owned, measured, and durable improvements.
About the Role
We are hiring an experienced infrastructure engineer to make ChatGPT development dramatically faster and more reliable. You will work across local development, build systems, CI, deployment infrastructure, test ownership, and production safety signals to reduce the time and attention required to move a healthy change from development to production.
This is not a narrow tooling role. The best person for this job will be comfortable diagnosing messy distributed systems, reading developer pain signals from Slack and metrics, building reliable automation, negotiating ownership across teams, and making tradeoffs between velocity and production safety. You should enjoy treating engineers as users and turning confusing workflow failures into clear, measured systems.
In this role, you will:
- Reduce local development startup and iteration latency for ChatGPT engineers
- Improve Bazel and build performance for local machines, devboxes, and CI, including cache effectiveness, reproducibility, disk usage, remote cache behavior, and observability into invalidations.
- Improve CI reliability and merge throughput by reducing unrelated failures, tail latency, flaky or mis-owned tests, quarantine friction, and repeated manual reruns.
- Build agents that help PRs make forward progress: rebasing, conflict resolution, CI triage, safe reruns, owner routing, and clear identification of external blockers.
- Make deploy pipelines more self-healing, especially when transient alerts, known-bad clusters, recovered synthetics, stale RCs, or noisy gates should not require human babysitting.
- Improve deploy observability so engineers can quickly tell where a change is, what is blocking it, whether the signal is trustworthy, and who owns the next action.
- Establish lightweight metrics for before-and-after impact, such as commit-to-prod latency, deploy-window throughput, CI tail latency, local bootup time, failure rates, manual interventions, false-positive gates, and developer-reported pain.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have strong experience with large-scale developer infrastructure, build systems, CI/CD, deployment systems, or production reliability.
- Can debug across local machines, devboxes, remote caches, monorepos, service dependencies, auth systems, and distributed deploy pipelines.
- Are comfortable with systems like Bazel, Buildkite, Kubernetes, Temporal, Python/TypeScript services, GitHub workflows, and large monorepo tooling, or can ramp quickly on equivalents.
- Think in product loops as much as systems loops: you care whether developers can understand and trust the workflow, not just whether a subsystem is technically healthy.
- Know how to replace repeated manual intervention with policy-backed automation while preserving production safety.
- Communicate well across teams and can turn ambiguous "this is slow/broken/flaky" reports into crisp owners, hypotheses, metrics, and shipped fixes.
- Prefer practical measurement over vibes, while still knowing that developer frustration is often the first signal of a real systems problem.
- Are energized by high-leverage work where a small improvement can save hundreds of engineering hours.
Nice to have:
- Experience improving developer experience in a very large monorepo.
- Experience with remote execution, remote caching, hermetic builds, or cache reproducibility.
- Experience designing CI quarantine, test ownership, merge queue, or auto-revert systems.
- Experience with progressive delivery, canary/preview/stable deploy pipelines, synthetics, alert quality, and deploy-manager style workflows.
- Experience building agent-assisted developer workflows, such as automated PR babysitting, CI triage, or conflict resolution.
- Familiarity with security and access-control constraints around secrets, internal auth, VPN/exit-node networking, and local development.

About the Team
Our team builds classification and evaluation systems that give post-training and research teams fast, reliable feedback on model behavior. We combine machine learning and production engineering to make these capabilities accurate, efficient, and useful at scale, helping researchers assess changes and improve models and products.
We work closely with researchers and data scientists and have broad ownership of the software that makes these capabilities available. Our work spans real-time systems, data engineering, model serving, and tools for experimentation, with careful attention to performance, reliability, and privacy.
About the Role
We’re looking for a software engineer to build and evolve our classification and evaluation platform. You’ll develop services, online and offline pipelines, and tools that help researchers and data scientists turn an idea into a working measurement and iterate on it quickly.
This role combines software and data engineering with hands-on production ownership. You’ll shape the architecture, deliver new capabilities, improve inference efficiency, and keep the system dependable as workloads and requirements evolve. Strong candidates will bring deep software engineering expertise and an interest in building a technical product in close partnership with its users.
In this role, you will:
- Design and build software services and APIs for configuring, running, and managing classifiers and evaluations.
- Build and operate online and offline classification pipelines that support reliable, efficient execution at scale.
- Improve model-serving performance, including throughput, latency, concurrency, and compute utilization.
- Build tools that make experimentation, debugging, and iteration straightforward for researchers and data scientists.
- Own production reliability, observability, and incident response, and reduce the operational burden of running the platform.
- Partner with machine learning engineers to bring new classification capabilities into production.
- Work closely with post-training researchers and data scientists to understand their workflows, identify high-impact improvements, and shape the product.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- Experience designing, building, and operating software services or distributed systems at scale.
- Strong fundamentals in API design, concurrency, caching, performance, and failure recovery.
- Ability to investigate complex production problems and make sound architectural tradeoffs.
- A track record of owning software from initial design through deployment and ongoing operation.
- Strong product judgment and an interest in working directly with technical users.
- Comfort with ambiguous problems and broad ownership across multiple parts of a system.
- Fluency in using AI agents to move quickly across multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.
- Interest in machine learning, data science, and statistics; experience with model serving, ML platforms, or inference optimization is a plus.

About the team
OpenAI is building a new generation of AI-powered consumer devices, creating opportunities to bring increasingly capable AI into people's everyday lives.
Our Data Engineering team is responsible for establishing the foundational data infrastructure that supports the development, manufacturing, launch, and ongoing operation of these products. We're building the systems that connect information across the entire device lifecycle, enabling engineering, operations, and Data Science partners to understand product performance, identify problems, and make better decisions.
This is an early-stage organization with significant greenfield opportunities. We're looking for engineers who want to shape the technical foundations of a rapidly growing business and establish systems that will scale alongside our products.
About the role:
As a Data Engineer, you'll design, build, and scale the data infrastructure that powers OpenAI's hardware and consumer devices organization.
You'll tackle technically challenging problems involving complex data sources, evolving operational requirements, and systems that need to scale from early development through manufacturing and consumer deployment.
Unlike roles focused primarily on supporting individual analytics projects, this position emphasizes building durable, reusable data foundations that enable multiple teams and use cases.
You'll have significant ownership over technical decisions, work closely with partners across engineering, manufacturing, operations, and Data Science, and help define how we approach Data Engineering as the organization grows.
In this role, you will:
- Build foundational data infrastructure: Design and implement reliable, scalable data pipelines, platforms, and datasets that support hardware development, manufacturing, customer operations, and device performance.
- Connect complex data ecosystems: Integrate information across manufacturing systems, factory operations, device telemetry, quality assurance, and customer-facing operational systems.
- Establish durable data models: Develop reusable datasets and data architectures that enable consistent measurement, investigation, and decision-making across multiple teams.
- Enable manufacturing and quality intelligence: Connect manufacturing conditions and production history with downstream product performance, reliability, returns, and failure signals.
- Prepare for scale: Design systems that evolve from early-stage development and initial production to increasingly complex operations and large-scale consumer deployment.
- Partner across disciplines: Work with hardware and software engineers, manufacturing teams, operations leaders, and Data Scientists to translate emerging requirements into robust technical solutions.
- Shape our technical direction: Help establish engineering standards, architectural principles, data quality practices, and infrastructure decisions that will influence the organization for years to come.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Are comfortable making architectural decisions as requirements evolve and the right solutions aren't immediately obvious.
- Are highly self-directed and can take broad, ambiguous problems from exploration through implementation.
- Enjoy working directly with cross-functional partners and understanding how technical decisions affect real products and operational outcomes.
- Have a builder's mentality and are energized by creating foundational systems rather than exclusively optimizing mature infrastructure.
- Hold a high bar for engineering quality while remaining pragmatic about the speed and flexibility required in an early-stage environment.
Minimum Qualifications:
- Have exceptional Data Engineering fundamentals and a track record of designing, building, and operating complex data systems.
- Bring strong technical judgment around data architecture, distributed systems, data modeling, reliability, and scalability.
- Have experience developing production-grade pipelines and infrastructure across heterogeneous data sources.
Bonus points if you have:
- Experience with hardware, consumer electronics, connected devices, or IoT.
- Experience building data infrastructure for manufacturing, factory operations, or supply-chain systems.
- Familiarity with device telemetry, reliability engineering, product quality, or failure analysis.
- Experience supporting customer operations, technical support, or Trust & Safety.
- A track record of building data platforms or foundational infrastructure in a startup or rapidly scaling organization.
Prior hardware experience is not required. We value exceptional engineering ability, intellectual curiosity, and the capacity to learn new domains quickly.

About the Team
OpenAI Presence, part of Enterprise Engineering, builds a platform for reliable AI agents that carry out high-volume business workflows. We focus on specific use cases such as customer support, sales, and insurance claims, helping organizations put agents to work in production.
The Presence platform supports the agent development lifecycle, including evaluation, deployment, and improvement through real interactions. It connects agents to company systems and supports voice and chat experiences, with policies, guardrails, and human handoffs to help businesses stay in control. Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.
About the Role
We’re looking for an engineer to help shape the foundations of Presence and build the systems that make AI agents dependable in everyday business operations. You’ll help set the platform’s technical direction while staying close to the code, taking architecture from early decisions through to systems that perform reliably at scale.
You’ll bring deep backend expertise and the product judgment to connect what we build with how businesses use it. The work centers on the services that power Presence and extends across the stack—giving you scope to shape both the underlying systems and the experiences they enable.
In this role, you will:
- Provide hands-on technical leadership, guiding architectural decisions and implementation across the Presence platform.
- Design and build backend systems for reliable, high-volume agent workflows in support, sales, and other enterprise use cases.
- Develop platform capabilities that support agent development and learning from real-world use.
- Identify and address reliability bottlenecks as agent workflows become more complex and usage grows.
- Work across backend infrastructure and product experiences as needed, collaborating with other engineers to turn evolving requirements into working software.
Your background might look something like:
- 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.
- A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.
- Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.
- End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.
- Strong production engineering judgment: you can diagnose difficult failures, reason about performance and scalability, and improve reliability through testing, observability, and operational discipline.
- Strong product judgment that connects technical decisions to user needs, with the ability to balance delivery speed, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability.
- The ability to move between backend infrastructure and product experiences, contribute across the stack when needed, and quickly learn unfamiliar systems, tools, and domains.
- Clear technical communication and effective collaboration across disciplines, including explaining trade-offs, creating alignment, and driving complex work forward while remaining hands-on.
- Experience with AI agents, enterprise workflows, integrations, or agent development and evaluation is a plus, but not required.

About the Team
Enterprise Controls & Console is part of Enterprise Engineering. We build the permissions, governance, and administration capabilities that help organizations use and deploy ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI products with confidence. We give administrators granular controls over access and security, helping ensure that people and agents operate within the boundaries their organizations define.
Our work combines complex backend platform engineering with enterprise product needs and touches every major product and model launch. We build scalable, reusable services and intuitive administration experiences, and provide a shared controls foundation that enables internal teams to introduce new capabilities safely.

We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to help shape and build the systems behind enterprise access, governance, and sharing. You will bring deep backend expertise and strong product judgment to problems that span multiple OpenAI products, including how people and agents share access and work together. You will lead technical design and delivery, translate ambiguous enterprise needs into clear system behavior, and remain hands-on from implementation through production operation. - Deep backend engineering expertise and a track record of shipping complex product or platform capabilities that customers depend on.
- Experience providing technical leadership for substantial initiatives, making architectural decisions, and coordinating delivery across teams while remaining hands-on.
- Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, Rust, Java, or C++, with sound software design and systems fundamentals.
- Experience designing distributed services, APIs, and data models, with an understanding of reliability, consistency, scalability, and performance tradeoffs.

About the Team
OpenAI’s People team helps us hire, support, and retain the people who will safely build and deploy artificial intelligence that benefits humanity.
The People Technology team brings together our enterprise people systems and the engineers building new internal products and AI-powered tools. We work across the People organization to improve the employee experience, simplify operations, and build technology that supports OpenAI’s global growth.
About the Role
We’re looking for a People Technology Analyst with deep expertise in Workday Absence, Time Tracking, and Benefits. You’ll independently own configuration, ongoing support, and improvements across these areas, including benefits for our US and international employees, from day one.
You’ll work closely with Benefits, People Operations, Payroll, Finance, and Engineering to translate complex requirements into reliable systems and straightforward employee experiences. You should be comfortable configuring Workday yourself, tracing issues across modules and integrations, and owning improvements from the first conversation through launch and ongoing support.
As part of our combined People Technology team, you’ll also help identify where automation, AI, and custom tools can improve how we work. You’ll bring the domain expertise needed to make those solutions useful and dependable.
In this role, you will:
- Own Workday configuration and improvements across Absence, Time Tracking, and Benefits, including the connections between leave, time worked, and benefits eligibility.
- Design and maintain absence plans, accruals, eligibility rules, leave processes, time entry rules, calculations, validations, and approvals for a growing global workforce.
- Partner with the Payroll systems owner to ensure absence, time tracking, and benefits data flows accurately into payroll. Investigate source data issues and test downstream impacts of changes in your areas.
- Independently own US and international benefits configuration, including benefit plans, eligibility rules, enrollment events, life events, coverage levels, and rates.
- Lead open enrollment systems readiness, including configuration, testing, launch, and support. Partner with technical teams and benefits vendors to maintain and troubleshoot integrations.
- Lead Absence, Time Tracking, and Benefits systems work for new countries and entities, policy changes, and evolving employee needs. Partner with functional owners to translate local requirements into configuration.
- Own projects from discovery and prioritization through configuration, testing, release, documentation, and adoption. Stay accountable for how the solution performs after launch.
- Partner with engineers to improve integrations and build automation or AI-assisted workflows that reduce manual work and make employee support easier.
- Maintain system security, data quality, reporting, and change controls. Resolve production issues and address their underlying causes.
- Create clear documentation and training that helps employees, managers, and People teams use our systems effectively.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- Deep, hands-on Workday expertise across Absence and Time Tracking, with experience designing, configuring, testing, and supporting connected workflows across both.
- Demonstrated experience independently owning Workday Benefits configuration for US and international programs, including open enrollment, eligibility, life events, and connections to benefits vendors.
- An understanding of how time, absence, and benefits data flows into payroll and other downstream systems, with the ability to test changes and troubleshoot issues with the relevant system owners.
- Experience translating complex policies and business requirements into maintainable system designs, including country-specific configurations.
- Strong Workday technical skills, including business processes, calculated fields, reporting, security, and data loads, along with the ability to troubleshoot integrations with technical partners.
- Ownership of systems through implementation and ongoing operations, with a record of improving reliability and the experience of the people using them.
- Good product judgment. You ask questions, understand the underlying problem, prioritize thoughtfully, and evaluate whether a change made things better.
- Clear communication and the ability to work across People, Payroll, Benefits, Finance, and Engineering.
- Comfort working through ambiguity, balancing urgent operational needs with longer-term improvements, and following through on details.
Preferred Qualifications
- Global Absence, Time Tracking, or Benefits implementations and new country or entity launches.
- Collaboration with software engineers on internal products, integrations, or workflow automation.
- Practical use of AI to improve systems work, documentation, testing, or employee support.
- Relevant Workday certifications or Workday Pro credentials.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Monetization team is a new cross-functional group spanning engineering, product, research, and design. We are building the foundational systems that will help OpenAI scale access to intelligence responsibly.
Our mission is to create user-first, privacy-preserving monetization products—including next-generation ads experiences—that strengthen trust, expand economic opportunity, and support OpenAI’s long-term innovation. We believe monetization should deliver clear user value, uphold rigorous privacy and safety standards, and sustain a healthy ecosystem for developers and businesses.
The team operates in a greenfield environment, moving quickly through prototyping, experimentation, and iterative deployment. We partner closely across Product, Design, and Research to bring new capabilities into real-world systems at global scale.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to lead the design and development of the systems that turn advertiser feeds (eg. retail feeds, travel feeds etc.) into relevant, reliably delivered ads. In this foundational role, you will build across the full ads lifecycle—from ingesting and organizing retailer or travel catalogs into efficient retrieval systems, supporting ranking models, and serving ads at scale.
This role is well suited to an engineer with direct experience in product ads retrieval, ranking, and delivery, along with a strong understanding of merchant feeds and shopping systems such as Google Shopping, YouTube product ads, or Amazon. We also welcome engineers with Senior Staff-level or greater scope who have deep ownership of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing, ads serving, or closely related distributed systems.
You will independently own complex systems, make sound technical tradeoffs, and help define the architecture and roadmap for Shopping/Travel/Feed Ads. You will collaborate closely with Ads ML, Ads Delivery, Product, Design, and Research to connect accurate, fresh advertiser feed information with useful ads experiences in ChatGPT.
This role is based in San Francisco and Mountain View. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL
- Design and build pipelines that ingest, validate, normalize, and refresh merchant product feeds, keeping catalog information accurate and available for serving.
- Develop scalable catalog storage and indexing systems that make large inventories searchable and reflect changes in product availability, pricing, and attributes.
- Build search and retrieval systems that efficiently identify relevant, eligible products across merchant catalogs.
- Partner with Ads ML to connect product retrieval with ranking models through dependable interfaces, features, and serving infrastructure.
- Engineer low-latency, high-throughput ads delivery systems with strong reliability and correctness guarantees.
- Design real-time event pipelines and distributed storage that support catalog freshness, serving decisions, and downstream feedback.
- Build observability and quality controls to detect feed errors, stale inventory, indexing delays, and serving issues.
- Define technical direction and drive complex projects from early prototypes through production deployment and operation.
- Operate systems with high engineering rigor through testing, monitoring, privacy and security reviews, and strong operational practices.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU
- Have extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, with direct ownership of product ads retrieval, ranking infrastructure, or delivery.
- Understand merchant feeds and shopping systems, including how catalog quality, product availability, and freshness affect relevance and ads performance.
- Have built systems for shopping or product ads at platforms such as Google Shopping, YouTube, Amazon, or a comparable environment.
- Alternatively, have operated at Senior Staff-level scope or above, leading the architecture and delivery of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing platforms, ads serving, or related backend systems.
- Have built low-latency, high-throughput services and data pipelines with demanding reliability and correctness requirements.
- Can reason across ingestion, storage, indexing, retrieval, ranking, and serving, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between freshness, relevance, latency, and cost.
- Are comfortable partnering with machine-learning teams to bring ranking models and signals into dependable production systems.
- Can define technical direction in an ambiguous 0→1 environment and independently drive complex work across teams.
- Communicate clearly and make technical decisions grounded in user value, merchant experience, and long-term system health.

The Plugin Developer Platform team builds the APIs, SDKs, and tools that let people extend ChatGPT and Codex. We work on plugins, connectors, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and interactive apps.
We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work covers plugin creation and publishing, the systems that run plugins across our products, and open standards that developers can build on.

We’re looking for an experienced Android engineer to bring plugins, connectors, and interactive apps to life on mobile. You’ll build the Android experiences and platform foundations that help developers extend ChatGPT and help users discover and use those capabilities from their devices.
You’ll work across native Android interfaces, developer-facing APIs, and the systems that support extensibility on mobile. You’ll collaborate closely with product, design, and platform engineers, owning features from early exploration through implementation, launch, and iteration.
You’ll also engage directly with developers and partners to understand how their workflows translate to Android. Their experience will inform the interfaces and abstractions you build, the problems you prioritize, and the tradeoffs you make.

- Partner with platform engineers to connect native mobile experiences with APIs, SDKs, and backend systems.
- Work with developers and partners to identify integration challenges and improve the experience of building for mobile.
- Improve app performance, reliability, architecture, testing, and developer tooling.
- Own projects from initial requirements through release, measurement, and iteration.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have deep experience building Android applications using Kotlin and modern Android development frameworks.
- Have shipped consumer-facing mobile products at scale and care deeply about performance, quality, and user experience.
- Bring a platform mindset and enjoy designing reusable interfaces and abstractions that other developers build on.
- Enjoy collaborating across engineering, product, and design, and working directly with developers and partners.
- Are excited about bringing AI-powered tools and extensible experiences to mobile.
- Thrive in fast-moving environments where you help define both product and technical direction.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. The OpenAI Life Sciences team works at the intersection of advancing frontier life sciences model capabilities and building products to help scientists accelerate their research and leverage the full potential of AI for scientific work.
We’re building platforms that connect model intelligence with practical scientific workflows. Our work covers workflows from next-gen sequencing analysis to designing new drugs, helping scientists run computational workloads as well as access laboratory services. By making these capabilities more accessible and useful, we aim to improve early discovery and support downstream progress in drug development.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for experienced full-stack product engineers with strong backend skills to join our growing Life Sciences team.
This is an individual contributor role with substantial ownership. You’ll help define products, design systems, and ship experiences that connect scientists with AI capabilities and laboratory workflows. You’ll work across the stack, partnering with researchers, scientists, and infrastructure engineers to turn complex needs into reliable, intuitive products.
We value strong engineering fundamentals, product judgment, and experience shipping to large user bases. Life sciences experience is helpful, but you don’t need a scientific background to make a meaningful contribution.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL
- Design backend services, APIs, and integrations that connect users with models, scientific tools, and laboratory services.
- Create intuitive interfaces that help scientists navigate complex workflows.
- Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, operation, and iteration.
- Work with scientific and research partners to identify user needs and prioritize valuable product improvements.
- Partner with dedicated infrastructure engineers on performance, reliability, and scaling.
- Make thoughtful engineering decisions that balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU
- Have strong software engineering fundamentals and depth in backend development, alongside the ability to build across the stack.
- Have shipped and operated products used by large user bases.
- Bring strong product sense and can translate ambiguous needs into useful software.
- Work autonomously, make sound technical decisions, and drive projects forward with limited direction.
- Enjoy hands-on building and taking ownership within a lean team.
- Are excited about advances in AI and how they could change scientific work.
- Learn unfamiliar domains quickly and collaborate effectively with scientific and technical partners.
PARTICULARLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE
- Building AI applications, model-serving integrations, or inference platforms.
- Developing marketplaces or products that coordinate services and complex workflows.
- Taking new products from early concepts through launch and adoption.
- Working with scientific tools, research data, or laboratory systems.

About the Team
OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.
About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.
You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.
Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.
This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.
In this role, you will:
- Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.
- Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier.
- Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.
- Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms.
- Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery.
- Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements.
- Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop.
- Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects.
- Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence.
- Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations.
- Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty.
- Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work.
- Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction.
- Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input.
- Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait.
- Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details.
- Learn exceptionally quickly, developing your understanding of AI training, evaluation and unfamiliar research areas to become a useful collaborator.
- We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area.

We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.
A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.
You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.
This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.
In This Role, You Will
- Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.
- Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.
- Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.
- Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.
- Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.
- Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.
- Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.
- Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.
- Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.
- Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.
- Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.
- Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.
- Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.
- Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.
Minimum Qualifications
- 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments
- Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have
- A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.
- Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.
- Experience developing one or more of the following:
- HSM firmware or trusted applications
- Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services
- HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware
- PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations
- Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols
- HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems
- Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary
- Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.
- Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.
- Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.
- Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.
- The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.
- Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.
Additional Experience That May Be Helpful
- Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.
- Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.
- Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.
- Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.
- Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.
- Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.
- Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.
- Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.
- Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.
- Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Frontier Assurance team strengthens OpenAI’s safety decisions through independent expertise, rigorous assessment, and public transparency. We coordinate external evaluations of frontier models and safeguards, develop approaches such as embedded auditing, and manage the misalignment disclosure process and safeguard testing. Our work helps independent experts scrutinize OpenAI’s safety approach and ensures their findings inform consequential decisions about advanced AI systems.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a researcher on Frontier Assurance, you will build the technical foundations for rigorous assessments of frontier AI risks. You will help design technical assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.
You will work closely with external evaluators and embedded auditors, helping them understand the systems they are assessing and access the models, data, and technical information their work requires. Where direct access is not possible, you will conduct experiments and analyses on their behalf, with methods and results they can meaningfully scrutinize.
This role combines research engineering, experimental design, and close technical collaboration. You will move between investigating specific safety questions, navigating complex internal systems, and building reusable tools that make assessments more thorough and efficient. Your work will help turn independent scrutiny into concrete evidence about model capabilities, safeguards, and remaining risks.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Help design assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.
- Support the technical execution of third-party assessments and embedded audits focused on frontier risks, working with evaluators to translate research questions into experiments, analyses, and evidence requirements.
- Pair closely with external researchers to provide the data, technical documentation, and context needed to assess models and safeguards. Help them understand relevant system behavior, configurations, and limitations.
- Design and implement secure access to assessment environments, working with research, engineering, and security teams to make relevant models, tools, and information available.
- Conduct experiments and run analyses on evaluators’ behalf when direct access is constrained. Develop methods collaboratively, document implementation choices, and make results reproducible and open to challenge.
- Build tooling that automates auditing, assessment workflows, and internal assurance work, including evidence collection, evaluation execution, and tracking changes across model or safeguard versions.
- Reproduce external findings, investigate discrepancies with internal results, and work with relevant teams to test proposed mitigations and identify unresolved questions.
- Document methods, findings, and limitations clearly so that evaluators and internal decision-makers can understand what the evidence establishes and where uncertainty remains.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have strong software engineering skills and experience building research tools, evaluation infrastructure, or systems for analyzing complex data.
- Have practical experience working with modern machine learning systems, including designing experiments, running evaluations, and interpreting results.
- Can navigate unfamiliar codebases and infrastructure, debug across system boundaries, and turn ambiguous research requests into reliable technical implementations.
- Bring sound judgment to experimental design and measurement, including identifying confounders, limitations, and gaps in evidence.
- Enjoy working closely with researchers, explaining technical systems, and helping others investigate difficult questions.
- Value independent scrutiny and can support rigorous assessments that challenge internal assumptions.
- Have an understanding of, or strong interest in, frontier AI risks, alignment, and the evaluation of safeguards.
Experience with AI safety evaluations, adversarial testing, security research, or technical auditing would be especially relevant.

About the Team
The Preparedness Engineering team is responsible for building and operating safeguards for frontier model risks, to safely enable advanced capabilities while detecting and limiting harm.
About the Role
We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead a team building software systems that detect and prevent harmful misuse of frontier AI models—before incidents occur. This is a builder’s role: you’ll lead engineers shipping production services, detection pipelines, and mitigation mechanisms that protect frontier model integrity and reduce high-severity misuse risk.
While this work intersects with frontier model development, security and risk, we’re explicitly seeking someone with a software engineering foundation who is comfortable building reliable systems that can operate at billions of users scale.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
- Lead a team of software engineers building detection + mitigation systems for frontier model harms.
- Set the technical roadmap and execution strategy: prioritize, design, ship, iterate, measure impact.
- Build production systems: services, pipelines, tooling, instrumentation, and automation that scale with frontier model usage.
- Partner deeply with Research and Product to translate evolving model capabilities into concrete tests, signals, and mitigations that can be deployed at scale.
- Drive strong engineering fundamentals: architecture, reliability, monitoring, performance, and operational excellence.
- Hire and grow an exceptional team across backend, data systems, and applied ML engineering domains as needed.
- Anticipate what breaks at scale as agentic workflows become more capable.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Experience building systems in adversarial, fast-evolving environments
- Thrive in high context environments
- Are comfortable with ambiguity and novelty
- Communicate clearly and build trust quickly with senior stakeholders—pragmatic, collaborative, and calm under scrutiny.
- Significant experience leading engineering teams and delivering production systems end-to-end.
- Strong technical judgment in system design, distributed systems, data pipelines, observability, and operational reliability.
- Demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally with Research/Product/Security to ship systems that materially reduce risk or abuse at scale.
- Background in autonomy, high-scale real-time systems, or intelligence-adjacent technical domains is a plus.

ABOUT THE TEAM
OpenAI’s Client Platform Engineering team builds and operates the platforms that make employee devices secure, reliable, and easy to use. Our work spans device posture and trust, onboarding, application delivery, operating-system updates, fleet telemetry, and employee-facing remediation. We partner with Security, IT, Research, Applied, and specialized engineering teams to reduce friction while protecting OpenAI’s systems and data.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Client Platform Engineer, You will build and own agentic solutions that automate OAI fleet operations and reduce employee friction, with measurable outcomes and reliability. You will develop first-party software, integrate commercial and open-source tools, and own changes from design and testing through deployment and production operations. Your work will improve security, reliability, and the employee experience.
We’re looking for people who are passionate about automation, endpoint security, and building scalable solutions that improve employee experience. You should have deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets at scale, with strong software engineering skills to automate security controls and fleet operations across environments with different compliance requirements. Your problem-solving mindset and attention to detail will be key to success in this role.
In this role, you will:
Build the platforms that help employees do their best work on devices they can trust.
- Own the design, development, deployment, and operation of secure Linux endpoint management systems across environments with different compliance requirements.
- Create magical employee experiences by building agentic workflows with OpenAI products and models that use fleet telemetry to anticipate issues, guide remediation, and design friction out of everyday work.
- Make new hires productive from day one, using OpenAI products to simplify device setup, software delivery, and onboarding support.
- Build secure, reliable workflows with scoped access, human review for sensitive changes, traceable actions, and tested recovery.
- Partner with IT, Security, Research, and Engineering to deliver consistent Linux provisioning, updates, and support alongside macOS and Windows.
- Develop first-party software and integrate commercial and open-source tools for software packaging, deployment, and application management.
- Manage fleet configuration as code through GitOps, version control, peer review, and automated validation.
- Build and operate CI/CD pipelines for fleet infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and GCP, with staged deployments and tested rollback.
- Use fleet telemetry to proactively improve performance and reliability, detect configuration drift, and verify deployment outcomes.
- Participate in engineering on-call, own incident resolution, and turn operational lessons into lasting improvements that reduce recurring failures and manual work.
YOU MAY BE A FIT FOR THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:
- Proficiency in Python, Go, or another modern programming language.
- Deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets with configuration management, MDM, device enrollment, policy enforcement, and cloud identity integration.
- Demonstrated success with open-source endpoint tools for configuration, device and application management, and telemetry.
- Experience delivering secure, reliable, scalable systems across different compliance requirements.
- Deep experience managing infrastructure at scale with IaC and GitOps, using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, and Chef.
- Experience integrating and operating fleet infrastructure with CI/CD and DevOps workflows.
- A track record of deploying and operating fleet infrastructure in public cloud environments (Azure, AWS, GCP).
- Initiative, analytical judgment, and the ability to turn problems into practical improvements.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:
- Deep experience with open-source fleet management tools and frameworks.
- Experience with containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
- Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and NIST.
- Strong soft skills, including stakeholder communication and cross-functional collaboration.
- Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CCSP.
- A security thought leader with contributions to CPE open-source projects or technical communities.

About the Team
Enterprise Security protects the systems, identities, devices, and services that enable OpenAI's employees to work securely and effectively. We partner across IT and Security to understand risk, build practical defenses, and support a rapidly evolving technical environment.
About the Role
We are looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer with a focus on vulnerability management, novel vulnerabilities, and zero-day response. You will investigate vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across networks, endpoints, and SaaS, prioritize them in the context of real exposure, and drive remediation through verified outcomes.
You will also build security capabilities and automation, use AI agents to solve practical problems, and help shape how enterprise security operates as agents become a larger part of everyday work.
This role is open to candidates in San Francisco, CA, and to remote candidates in the United States.
In this role, you will:
- Discover, investigate, and prioritize vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across enterprise systems, including novel vulnerabilities and zero-days with incomplete information and no established playbook.
- Translate technical findings into clear attack paths, business impact, and actionable remediation.
- Develop and validate emergency mitigations when patches are unavailable, coordinate with system owners, vendors, and incident responders, and drive durable fixes through verified closure.
- Improve asset visibility, ownership, vulnerability data quality, and reporting.
- Build and operate security tools and integrations using code, APIs, automation, and AI agents.
- Design controls for agent access, execution, and accountability.
- Contribute across endpoint, network, identity, and SaaS security, and support incident investigations when needed.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have independently investigated novel or emerging vulnerabilities and driven enterprise remediation from uncertain initial reports through mitigation and verified closure.
- Bring technical depth in a relevant security domain and working knowledge across networks, endpoints, and SaaS.
- Can understand and improve code and safely integrate APIs and security systems.
- Have solved substantive problems using AI agents and can explain how you evaluated and corrected their work.
- Think clearly about security tradeoffs, ambiguous evidence, and the changing risks of agentic systems.
- Collaborate effectively, take ownership, and communicate technical risk to varied audiences.

About the team
OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.
About the role
Forward Deployed Engineers lead complex deployments of frontier models in production. You will embed with customers where model performance matters, delivery is urgent, and ambiguity is the default. You will use this to map their problems, structure delivery, and ship fast.
As a Forward Deployed Engineer for AI Infra, you will work directly with customer engineers, researchers and product engineers on optimization problems across semiconductors and AI infrastructure. You will write and debug software, run experiments against real workloads and hardware, and improve the tools and product used across engagements.
You will help define the problem and success criteria, build the software needed to test an approach, and stay with the work through validation and deployment. Work may include inference performance and chip-design optimization. Success means producing results that stand up to correctness and performance checks, and contributing improvements that other engagements can use.
Success in this role means owning the delivery state across workstreams. You will hold the bar on quality and pace and help OpenAI learn through execution.
This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.
In this role, you will:
- Own technical delivery for agreed semiconductor and AI-infrastructure workstreams, from initial scoping and prototypes through validation, production deployment and adoption.
- Work closely with customer engineers to understand their workflows and constraints, define workloads, baselines and success criteria, and help what you build become part of how they work.
- Scope and sequence delivery, identify dependencies and blockers early, and make practical trade-offs between scope, speed and quality as the work develops.
- Personally build and debug production-quality software, including harnesses, integrations and product features that apply frontier models to problems in chip design, verification, inference and performance engineering.
- Design reproducible experiments, evaluations, graders and benchmarks to test approaches, validate correctness and performance, and establish whether improvements hold up in real engineering environments.
- Investigate model behavior and failure modes alongside researchers, contributing evaluation or training data and targeted experiments where they can improve the underlying capability.
- Contribute directly to core product development, working with product engineers to resolve tooling gaps, ship useful improvements and bring field learning into product decisions.
- Lead technical discussions and maintain alignment across customer, Product and Research teams. Build the domain and product fluency to explain capabilities, limitations and results, and keep ownership, risks and next steps clear.
- Turn successful approaches into reusable software, tools and playbooks, reducing the effort needed for future engagements and helping customer teams operate what has been built.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Bring 5+ years of engineering or technical deployment experience that includes customer-facing work
- Have scoped and delivered complex systems in fast-moving or ambiguous environments
- Write and review production-grade software, and debug unfamiliar systems across code, integrations and runtime behavior.
- Have built or deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behaviour affects product experience
- Simplify complexity and make fast, sound decisions under pressure
- Communicate clearly with engineers, product teams, and customer stakeholders
- Spot risks early and adjust without slowing down
- Model calm and judgment when the stakes are high
- Have a strong product sense and have contributed towards productizing efforts
- Have hands-on experience with applied machine learning, model evaluation, data quality, experimentation, or model-behavior analysis
- Can turn an ambiguous technical problem into a clear evaluation, a credible baseline, and a reproducible experiment
- Are comfortable learning unfamiliar technical domains and working closely with researchers, product engineers and customer engineers. Experience in semiconductor development, data-center systems or inference engineering is helpful.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Inference team brings OpenAI’s most capable research and technology to the world through our products. We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they’ve never been able to before. We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.
You’ll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation. We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.
- Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.
- Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.
- Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.
- Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.
- Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.
- Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.
- Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.
- Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.
- Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.
- Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.
- Have experience with quantization or attention kernels, which would be especially useful in this role.

GTM Systems builds and operates the tools that help our teams serve customers. We turn operational needs into reliable workflows, integrations, and automation so support teams can focus on helping customers.
About the role
We’re looking for a highly autonomous systems engineer to own and improve the systems that support our government work, including Salesforce and related integrations. Government systems will be your primary focus, with opportunities to contribute to other priorities.
You’ll build the platforms and workflows our support teams rely on, including Salesforce Service Cloud. The work spans new capabilities, ongoing maintenance, automation, and reliability.
You’ll identify needs, clarify scope, make technical decisions, and carry work through implementation, testing, production validation, and ongoing operation. You’ll work closely with government, support, operations, Security, and engineering partners to understand constraints and deliver systems that work well in practice.
In this role, you'll:
- Own government support systems from problem definition through design, delivery, production validation, and ongoing operation. Turn ambiguous needs into clear priorities and practical technical plans.
- Design and build maintainable service workflows, data models, interfaces, and integrations.
- Partner with government, support, operations, security, and engineering teams to make technical tradeoffs and translate access, data-handling, and change-control requirements into working solutions.
- Improve reliability and performance through automated tests, observability, safe releases, incident response, and recovery. Validate changes in production and address recurring failure modes.
- Document architecture, operational procedures, and recovery paths so systems are understandable and supportable. Automate repetitive work and contribute to other GASS priorities as needed.

- Prior experience delivering or operating systems in a government environment is required. You can explain how operational, access, or change-control constraints shaped your engineering decisions.
- Deep Salesforce Service Cloud experience, including Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, data modeling, configuration, and integrations. Sound judgment about when to use code or declarative automation.
- A track record of owning ambiguous technical work independently: identifying needs, defining scope, coordinating partners, making decisions, and following through after launch.
- Strong software engineering fundamentals: clear architecture, readable code, automated tests, and familiarity with languages such as Python or Java.
- Experience with Salesforce security and permissions, appropriate data handling, production reliability, incident response, and recovery.
- A strong understanding of support workflows and the ability to translate operational needs into maintainable systems. Clear communication and sound judgment about when to involve partners or escalate a decision.
- Preferred: relevant Salesforce certifications, such as Platform Developer II, Service Cloud Consultant, Platform App Builder, or Application Architect.
- Preferred: experience applying AI or automation to support operations.

About the role
We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.
You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.
You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.
In this role, you will:
- Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.
- Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.
- Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.
- Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.
- Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.
- Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.
- Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.
- Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.
- The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.
- Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.
- Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.
Helpful experience
Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.
