ABOUT THE TEAM
The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.
The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search. You’ll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneous, unstructured and semi-structured web content, making that information more accessible and useful to AI models.
The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information? How can we extract it reliably at web scale? And how do we measure whether it improves the model’s ability to reason and answer questions? How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?
You’ll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved. This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Develop methods to extract and connect structured information across diverse web sources, including entities, attributes, and relationships.
- Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.
- Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.
- Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.
- Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE
- Deep experience in knowledge extraction, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or related work that derives structure from large, heterogeneous datasets.
- Strong machine learning and research skills, with experience developing and evaluating methods for real-world data.
- A track record of building or scaling data and ML systems, particularly for web-scale extraction, indexing, or retrieval.
- Experience independently driving open-ended technical problems from an initial idea through experimentation and implementation.
- A first-principles approach to using AI and compute, with a willingness to rethink established methods as model capabilities improve.
- A strong interest in how the representation of information shapes what models can find, understand, and use.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.
The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information. In close partnership with researchers, we bring modeling advances into production and improve how AI systems discover, retrieve, and use knowledge.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for a Researcher to lead our safety and alignment research: building the systems that distinguish useful web content from spam, manipulation, and other adversarial or low-quality material.
The challenge extends beyond evaluating individual pages. A page may appear credible in isolation, while its links, metadata, or relationships with other sites reveal coordinated manipulation. As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.
You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Define the technical direction for Safety + Integrity, identifying gaps and determining which problems and interventions to prioritize.
- Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.
- Discover useful signals across page content, links, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.
- Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.
- Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.
- Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE
- Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.
- Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.
- An understanding of how adversaries manipulate content and links, coordinate across sites, and adapt to detection systems.
- A track record of independently defining ambiguous technical problems and driving solutions from experimentation through production.
- Experience working across research, engineering, and integrity teams while remaining hands-on with technical work.
- A first-principles approach to using frontier models and compute, and a strong interest in keeping detection systems effective as adversaries evolve.

ABOUT THE TEAM
OpenAI's Safety Research organization works to ensure that our most capable AI models can be deployed safely and responsibly. As frontier models become increasingly capable and autonomous, developing reliable ways to monitor their behavior, identify emerging risks, and evaluate the effectiveness of safety systems becomes increasingly important.
Our work focuses on advancing the research and evaluation methods needed to understand model behavior and ensure that monitoring systems remain effective as model capabilities evolve. We combine rigorous empirical research with practical safety interventions, working closely with research, engineering, and deployment teams to translate findings into improvements across OpenAI's models and products.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We are looking for a senior researcher to lead technical work on misalignment monitoring for frontier AI systems. You will develop methods to evaluate the effectiveness of AI monitors, understand their limitations, and improve our ability to detect and stop concerning model behavior reliably.
This role combines research leadership with hands-on technical execution. You will set research priorities, design rigorous evaluations, investigate monitoring failures, and develop approaches for stress-testing and improving monitoring systems. A key focus will be understanding where monitors produce false positives, miss important behaviors, or become less effective as models grow more capable.
You will work closely with researchers and engineers across OpenAI to turn monitoring research into practical improvements to our safety systems. We are looking for someone with strong research judgment, technical depth, and the ability to independently drive ambiguous problems from initial investigation through measurable results.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Lead the research and technical direction for evaluating and improving the misalignment monitoring of frontier AI systems.
- Design and execute rigorous evaluations that measure monitor effectiveness, identify failure modes, and assess the reliability of monitoring signals.
- Develop methods to stress-test and red-team monitors, including identifying behaviors that evade detection or expose weaknesses in existing approaches.
- Investigate false positives, missed detections, and other monitoring failures to improve the accuracy and usefulness of safety evaluations.
- Build scalable evaluation frameworks and experimental tools that enable ongoing measurement of monitoring performance as model capabilities evolve.
- Translate research findings into actionable improvements, working with partner teams to strengthen monitoring systems and inform broader safety decisions.
- Establish research priorities and guide technical execution, balancing foundational research questions with practical deployment needs.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have a strong background in machine learning research, particularly in model evaluations, AI safety, alignment, robustness, or related areas.
- Have demonstrated the ability to lead technically challenging research projects, from identifying important questions through designing experiments and delivering results.
- Bring strong experimental judgment and understand how to design evaluations that are rigorous, reproducible, and difficult to game.
- Have hands-on experience building or evaluating machine learning systems, including working with large language models or other frontier AI systems.
- Enjoy investigating complex failure modes and developing methods to distinguish meaningful safety signals from misleading measurements.
- Are comfortable working on open-ended research problems where the right methodology or success criteria may not be obvious at the outset.
- Combine strong research instincts with practical engineering ability and can independently build experiments, analyze results, and iterate quickly.
- Communicate technical findings clearly and enjoy collaborating across research, engineering, and safety teams.
- Are motivated by OpenAI's mission and the challenge of developing reliable oversight mechanisms for increasingly capable AI systems.
NICE TO HAVE:
- Experience with AI monitoring, automated evaluations, adversarial testing, or red-teaming.
- Research experience in scalable oversight, AI control, model behavior analysis, or interpretability.
- Experience developing monitoring or evaluation systems that are used in real-world deployments.
- A track record of technical research leadership, including mentoring researchers or coordinating cross-functional research initiatives.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Connector Ecosystem team builds the platform and product experiences that let people extend ChatGPT and Codex. We work on plugins, skills, connectors, interactive apps, and open standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We make plugins easy to discover, install, and use, ensure they’re invoked at the right time, and help people find new ways to get value from them.
We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work spans creation and publishing, reliable execution across our products, clear permissions and approvals, and the controls admins need to bring plugins to their organizations. We work closely with research to improve tool quality as models evolve.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for a product-minded Principal Software Engineer to set technical direction, build the systems behind plugins, and improve how models use them. Depending on your focus, you may scale generalist infrastructure and identity-related integrations across products, improve plugin quality at the intersection of backend engineering and applied AI, or work on the product experience itself to drive plugin usage. You’ll lead complex initiatives across teams and own problems from diagnosis and design through implementation and release.
You’ll remain hands-on while driving product and design decisions alongside Product, Design, Research, and engineering partners. You’ll help shape what we build and how it works, translate user and developer needs into clear priorities, and guide technical decisions that balance rapid iteration with long-term reliability and maintainability.
This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL
- Set technical direction and lead complex initiatives across the Plugin Ecosystem, aligning architecture and execution across teams.
- Drive product and design decisions with cross-functional partners, helping define priorities and shape intuitive experiences for users and developers.
- Design and ship APIs, SDKs, and services that developers use to extend ChatGPT and Codex.
- Build intuitive experiences that help users discover, install, and use plugins to get more done.
- Make plugins easier to create, test, publish, update, and share.
- Improve when and how models use plugins, from choosing the right plugin to completing a task. Work with Research to diagnose failures and measure improvements as models evolve.
- Improve plugin reliability and interaction quality across ChatGPT and Codex, including interactive apps, with clear error messages and recovery paths.
- Build consistent permissions, approvals, and admin controls that help individuals and organizations confidently adopt plugins.
- Work with developers and partners to turn recurring problems into improvements to the platform, tooling, and documentation.
- Collaborate across engineering, Product, Research, Security, and Trust & Safety to scale plugin infrastructure and deliver safe, reliable execution.
- Raise the engineering bar through mentorship, thoughtful code reviews, and clear technical guidance.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU
- Have 10+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of building and shipping products or platforms that people and developers rely on.
- Have led complex technical initiatives across teams and driven product and design decisions in close partnership with product managers and designers.
- Care about product quality and can make complex capabilities feel intuitive, from discovering a useful plugin to completing a task with it.
- Have strong opinions about APIs and abstractions, and can explain the tradeoffs behind your decisions. Experience with identity, permissions, or integration-heavy systems is especially valuable.
- Enjoy talking with users and developers, understanding what they’re trying to accomplish, and turning recurring problems into product and platform improvements.
- Can move between product questions and technical details, collaborate across teams, and take an ambiguous problem through to production.
- Are comfortable working across web interfaces and backend systems. Experience building applied AI systems, diagnosing model–tool interactions, and measuring reliability and quality is especially valuable.
- Have built products people rely on or software that other developers use, such as an API or SDK, an open-source project, a developer platform, or internal tools with real users.

About the Team
OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products.
As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale.
About the Role
We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure.
In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone.
You will be involved in everything from physical network design and circuit provisioning to troubleshooting complex connectivity issues across Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3. You will play a critical role in expanding our network footprint, bringing new PoPs online, and ensuring that our infrastructure operates reliably as OpenAI continues to grow.
We're looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the infrastructure, thrive on solving difficult networking problems, and bring an automation-first mindset to scaling network operations.
In This Role, You Will:
- Design, deploy, and support WAN infrastructure across data centers, network PoPs, and cloud connectivity environments.
- Own the end-to-end activation and turn-up of network circuits, working directly with fiber carriers and cloud service providers to establish and validate connectivity.
- Troubleshoot complex network issues across physical, Layer 2, and Layer 3 infrastructure, including optical signal problems, FEC errors, routing issues, and connectivity failures.
- Diagnose and isolate network failures across carrier, cloud provider, and internal infrastructure boundaries, driving issues through resolution.
- Contribute to physical network infrastructure design, including port mappings, fiber and cable layouts, optical distribution frames (ODFs), and connectivity planning.
- Monitor network health, circuit utilization, and performance to proactively identify capacity constraints and reliability risks.
- Build automation and tooling to streamline network provisioning, deployment validation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows.
- Collaborate with network engineering, data center infrastructure, and external service providers to support the expansion of OpenAI's global backbone.
- Participate in an on-call rotation to maintain the reliability and availability of critical network infrastructure.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You:
- Have hands-on experience deploying, activating, and troubleshooting WAN circuits with telecommunications carriers, fiber providers, or cloud service providers.
- Have a strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including optical networking, Ethernet, TCP/IP, BGP, and Layer 2/3 connectivity.
- Are comfortable debugging network issues across multiple layers, from physical fiber connectivity and optical errors to routing and traffic forwarding.
- Have experience working with data center networking, carrier infrastructure, cloud interconnects, or large-scale WAN environments.
- Understand physical network infrastructure concepts such as fiber cabling, port mappings, optical distribution frames, and network equipment connectivity.
- Can independently investigate ambiguous connectivity problems, isolate root causes, and work across internal and external teams to restore service.
- Have experience with scripting or automation tools and are motivated to reduce manual work through repeatable, scalable processes.
- Enjoy working directly with infrastructure and take pride in owning technical problems from initial deployment through operational resolution.
- Thrive in a fast-moving environment where infrastructure requirements evolve rapidly and engineering decisions have a direct impact on global scale.
Nice to Have
- Experience building or operating large-scale backbone networks, hyperscale data center networks, or cloud provider interconnect infrastructure.
- Familiarity with optical transport technologies, network telemetry, and advanced troubleshooting of physical network links.
- Experience automating network operations using Python, Go, or infrastructure automation frameworks.
- Experience deploying new network PoPs or supporting large-scale network expansion projects.
- Experience collaborating with carriers, colocation providers, and cloud networking teams on complex connectivity deployments.
Why This Role Matters
OpenAI's ability to advance AI research and deliver products at global scale depends on reliable, high-performance infrastructure.
As a member of the Global Network Infrastructure team, you will help build the connectivity foundation supporting some of the world's most demanding compute environments. Your work will directly contribute to expanding OpenAI's global network footprint, bringing critical infrastructure online, and ensuring the reliability of the systems powering frontier AI.
This is an opportunity to work on challenging infrastructure problems, take meaningful ownership of global network deployments, and help shape the next generation of OpenAI's network backbone.

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The ChatGPT team works across research, engineering, product, and design to bring OpenAI’s technology to the world. We serve a diverse audience of users who are already using ChatGPT daily in their lives and work.
We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.
About the role
We’re looking for a Content Designer to join OpenAI’s Content Design team, bringing deep expertise in prompt engineering and AI evaluation alongside strong content design craft and product judgment.
You’ll combine editorial judgment, product strategy, and technical implementation to build prompts, evaluations, and tools that help us create and improve content and messaging at scale. Your primary focus will be experiences that help people discover ChatGPT’s value, get started, and stay engaged—including notifications—with contributions to broader Content Design work as team needs evolve.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

- Shape content strategy for experiences that help people discover ChatGPT’s value, get started, and return to meaningful uses of the product.
- Design, implement, and iterate on prompt frameworks that guide AI-generated product content and messaging.
- Define content quality standards and build evaluation systems, datasets, and reviewer guidance that combine human judgment with automated assessments.
- Shape tools and workflows for generating, reviewing, and improving content across experiments and product experiences.
- Analyze model outputs and evaluation results to diagnose problems and improve content systems as models, products, and user needs evolve.
- Partner with product, engineering, design, research, and data science to connect content quality with user understanding, trust, engagement, and retention.
- Document reusable approaches and coach other Content Designers in developing prompts, defining evaluation criteria, and interpreting results.

- Bring 5+ years of experience in content design, content engineering, or a related discipline, with a track record of delivering work across complex product areas.
- Have hands-on experience developing prompts for shipped generative AI experiences and understand model capabilities, limitations, and failure patterns.
- Have designed and implemented content evaluation frameworks—and validated how reliably they assess quality.
- Have hands-on experience using code and APIs to build repeatable generation and evaluation workflows, and can partner with Engineering to integrate them into production.
- Bring strong writing, editorial judgment, and content strategy skills that you can apply across product experiences.

We work across product, growth, and monetization to help people get more value from OpenAI’s products. We identify opportunities for machine learning, build and test early solutions, and partner with engineering and product to bring successful approaches into production.
About the Role
We’re looking for a data scientist who can enter an unfamiliar product area, find a useful ML application, and turn it into a working product intervention. You will own the work from problem definition and data preparation through modeling, experimentation, and launch evaluation.
Projects will include personalization, next-best-action recommendations, lifecycle management, promotion targeting, and models of retention and customer lifetime value. You will help identify opportunities, build proofs of concept, evaluate, and iterate.
In this role, you will:
- Identify opportunities with product and business partners, define the decision a model will inform, and prioritize work by user value, feasibility, and expected impact.
- Build datasets, features, reproducible training workflows, and models. You’ll use a combination of tools appropriate to the task at hand.
- Translate predictions into product actions. Design experiments and use causal reasoning to establish whether those actions improve user and business outcomes.
- Partner with engineers on integration, serving or batch scoring, monitoring, and rollout. Stay involved through launch and iteration.
- Explain results and limitations clearly, document decisions, and build reusable methods that other teams can adopt.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have built and evaluated applied ML systems that influenced a product or business decision, with clear ownership of the modeling work.
- Write effective Python and SQL and can investigate imperfect data, debug models, and make pragmatic implementation choices.
- Build and schedule production scoring pipelines using dbt, airflow, and flyte.
- Understand supervised learning, evaluation, experimentation, and the difference between predicting an outcome and changing it.
- Can scope ambiguous problems, work across disciplines, and explain technical tradeoffs to colleagues with different backgrounds.
- Are motivated by helping people use AI effectively and by learning unfamiliar product domains.
- Are excited to take on challenging, impactful ML problems across multiple areas.
- Have experience with recommendation systems, personalization, growth, retention, lifetime value, or treatment-effect modeling would be useful. We welcome candidates whose relevant experience comes from other domains.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Physical Engineering team sits within OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. We’re exploring how frontier AI can help people design, simulate, and build better physical products—shortening development cycles, improving product performance, and expanding what engineering teams can accomplish.
Our initial focus is on mechanical and electrical engineering. We’re building experiences within ChatGPT and integrations with engineering software to help engineers move from early concepts through design, simulation, and preparation for production.
We operate as a small founding team within OpenAI, working directly with customers and closely with research, design, and forward deployed engineers. We learn by building, putting products in users’ hands, and using their feedback to guide our next steps.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Founding Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll help define and build the product and technical foundations of this new vertical. You’ll work across frontend experiences, backend services, and integrations to bring AI into complex engineering workflows.
You’ll combine strong software engineering fundamentals with product judgment and an eye for intuitive user experiences. Working directly with engineers and design partners, you’ll identify valuable problems, prototype solutions, and develop them into reliable products.
We’re particularly interested in engineers who have built CAD, CAE, simulation, or other engineering design software. You should be comfortable owning work independently, making decisions with incomplete information, and moving between product details and system architecture.
This is an opportunity to shape a new product area from its earliest stages, with significant influence over what we build, how it works, and the team we become.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Build and ship full-stack AI products that help mechanical and electrical engineers work through design and simulation tasks.
- Own projects from customer discovery and prototyping through production deployment and iteration.
- Create intuitive interfaces that help users understand, inspect, and refine complex engineering outputs.
- Develop backend services, APIs, plugins, and integrations that connect OpenAI models with engineering software.
- Work directly with customers to understand engineering constraints, identify valuable applications, and translate specific needs into broadly useful products.
- Partner with research, design, platform, and forward deployed engineering teams to bring emerging AI capabilities into practical workflows.
- Evaluate quality and reliability, using customer feedback and product evidence to understand whether we’re improving how engineers work.
- Help establish the technical foundations and engineering practices of a growing team.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have independently built and shipped substantial software products, with ownership across frontend and backend systems.
- Bring strong product instincts and UI judgment, especially for tools that make complex work easier to understand and perform.
- Enjoy working directly with users and translating their needs into thoughtful product and technical decisions.
- Can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear starting point and a working product.
- Move quickly, make pragmatic tradeoffs, and stay accountable for quality after launch.
- Learn unfamiliar tools and domains quickly and communicate clearly across disciplines.
- Are excited about applying frontier AI to the design and development of physical products.
PARTICULARLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE
- Building CAD, CAE, simulation, electrical design, or related professional software.
- Developing interactive tools for visual, spatial, or technically complex workflows.
- Connecting engineering tools through APIs, plugins, or extensions.
- Building AI-powered applications and evaluating their usefulness and reliability.
- Taking a product from concept to production as a founder or early engineer.

About the Team
We believe that increasing compute is a huge lever to AI progress.
The Hardware Systems team owns the design, development, and sourcing of the compute, storage and interconnect hardware needed to build OpenAI’s supercomputers at the scale needed to deliver AGI that is beneficial to humanity. This includes:
- Optimizing the processing hardware for AI models
- Developing and optimizing the end-to-end software stack
- Designing hardware systems to keep up with the needs of training and inference
- Enabling the scale-up and scale-out interconnect fabrics create the world’s most power supercomputers
We work at the very cutting edge of speed and scale. You won’t encounter another organization with as much compute per employee. We are a small team that moves quickly with access to huge resources. Our work has a direct impact on the success of OpenAI and, by extension, the field of AI as a whole.
About the Role
As the 1P Systems Lab Technical Program Manager, you will bring Lab infrastructure development knowledge and TPM experience to build out industry leading lab environments which are key to developing products and bringing the hardware roadmap to life. You’ll navigate an array of technical and partnership challenges as you work to develop our existing lab locations and deliver new sites on schedule. We’re looking for people excited to push the frontiers of computing and passionate about building.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

- Manage the end-to-end Lab strategy ensuring we have capacity and capabilities in place to successfully deliver the product roadmaps.
- Work cross-functionally and with external general contractors to develop and deliver new Lab facilities on schedule.
- Leveraging your Lab and datacenter construction technical knowledge to influence Lab design, including making trade-offs with internal and external partners.
- Manage on-going lab availability to ensure lab facilities and capabilities are in place to support product bring-up, debug activities, and all on-going development work
- Coordinate and lead internal resources and communication for efficient interaction with partners and vendors.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have experience leading high-power Lab or Datacenter design programs as a Technical Program Manager or Engineer from site selection to completion.
- Data center infrastructure and product knowledge (e.g. server, GPU, TPU, networking, storage), including product development (NPI) processes.
- Knowledge of Lab infrastructure equipment requirements to support product development.
- Experience taking products from concept to volume in a data center environment, ensuring the systems scale with high quality.
- Are eager to help design some of the world’s largest supercomputing systems, working at the edge of complex hardware challenges.
- Enjoy working with and enabling world-class AI Researchers and Engineers.
- Are passionate about the technical program function and enjoy independently owning and delivering on your teams’ goals and cutting-edge problems in AI compute.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Infranomics team builds the software and data foundations that help OpenAI understand, plan, and improve the economics of its infrastructure. The team works across engineering and finance to make infrastructure spend visible, allocate capacity effectively, and improve efficiency as our products grow.
Our systems support the CPU, network, storage and GPU infrastructure behind products such as ChatGPT, the API, and Codex. We are expanding these foundations to connect resource usage, cost, forecasting, and planning so teams can make better decisions at scale.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We are looking for a Software Engineer to lead the design, implementation, and operation of systems for infrastructure cost and efficiency. You will build the platforms that explain where infrastructure spend goes, identify opportunities to improve utilization, and help teams plan the capacity they need.
We ideally want direct experience building and operating software for infrastructure economics, such as usage metering, cost attribution, resource efficiency, budgeting, forecasting, or capacity planning. You should have owned systems that connect compute, storage, or network consumption to cost and help teams make measurable efficiency and investment decisions.
You will set technical direction for a growing area while staying close to the code. Working with infrastructure engineers, product teams, finance, and leadership, you will turn ambiguous business and engineering problems into reliable software, shared data, and measurable improvements. This role offers substantial autonomy and the opportunity to shape how OpenAI manages its infrastructure investment.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; or New York City, NY. This is an on-site role.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Define the technical direction and roadmap for infrastructure cost and efficiency systems, and lead projects from problem definition through implementation, adoption, and ongoing operation.
- Build billing, usage metering, and cost attribution systems that connect infrastructure spend to resources, workloads, services, and the teams that own them.
- Develop data pipelines and shared data models that combine cloud billing, resource inventory, and utilization signals into a dependable view of cost and capacity.
- Build tools for budgeting, forecasting, and capacity planning that help teams anticipate demand, allocate resources, and inform procurement decisions.
- Identify underutilized resources and other sources of waste, then partner with engineering teams to deliver and measure improvements while preserving performance and reliability.
- Create APIs, reporting tools, and automated controls that help teams understand their consumption, manage budgets, and make informed infrastructure tradeoffs.
- Provide technical leadership across teams, mentor engineers, and own the correctness, scalability, and production behavior of the systems you build.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have over 7 years of experience designing, building, and operating production software and distributed systems, with technical ownership across multiple teams or a significant infrastructure domain.
- Have built systems for infrastructure efficiency, cloud cost attribution, usage metering, budgeting, forecasting, or capacity management, and can connect that work to measurable outcomes.
- Remain a hands-on engineer who can move between architecture, implementation, debugging, and operational improvements.
- Understand how compute, storage, and networking consumption translate into cost, and can reason about the tradeoffs among utilization, performance, reliability, and growth.
- Care deeply about data correctness and can build trustworthy systems from complex billing and operational data.
- Work effectively across engineering, finance, product, and leadership, translating broad goals into a clear plan and driving adoption without relying on formal authority.
- Thrive with substantial autonomy, take ownership of loosely defined problems, and make pragmatic decisions as requirements evolve.
- Have experience building internal platforms that give engineering teams visibility into cloud spend, resource utilization, and ownership.
- Have experience developing batch or streaming data pipelines, financial data platforms, or large-scale analytics systems.
- Have experience with Kubernetes, public cloud infrastructure, or resource management systems across cloud and on-premises environments.
- Have experience automating resource allocation, cost allocation policies, budget tracking, or capacity forecasting.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and the API. Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.
Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering. We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You’ll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI’s products and services across clouds and regions. The team’s work spans L3, L4, and L7—from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.
You’ll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works. Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.
This role combines software engineering with production ownership. You’ll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.
- Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.
- Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.
- Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.
- Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.
- Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.
- Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.
- Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have 5+ years of experience building production infrastructure or distributed systems, including substantial work on networking or traffic infrastructure.
- Have depth in one or more areas such as cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, proxies and gateways, service meshes, load balancing, or global traffic routing.
- Understand networking fundamentals and can reason about how IP routing, TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT, TLS, and HTTP/gRPC affect connectivity and performance.
- Have hands-on experience building or operating systems such as Envoy, NGINX, Istio, Cilium, or comparable networking infrastructure.
- Write production software in Go, Rust, C++, Python, or a similar language, and use software and automation to solve operational problems.
- Can investigate unfamiliar failures using evidence, test hypotheses, and follow problems through to a verified resolution.
- Take ownership of design, implementation, rollout, and ongoing reliability, and communicate clearly across teams when a problem crosses ownership boundaries.
- Care about making infrastructure secure and understandable for the engineers who depend on it.
We value deep expertise and the willingness to learn across boundaries. You do not need prior experience with every technology or networking layer listed above.

About the Team
The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization.
Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.
Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.
About the Role
We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.
We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.
In this role, you will
- Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.
- Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.
- Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.
- Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.
- Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.
- Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.
- Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.
- Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.
You might thrive in this role if you
- Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.
- Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.
- Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.
- Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.
- Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.
- Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.
- Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.
If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

About the Team
Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.
About the Role
In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.
A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.
In This Role, You Will:
- Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.
- Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.
- Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.
- Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.
- Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You:
- Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.
- Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.
Qualifications
- Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.
- Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.
- Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.
- Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

About the Team
Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models, ensuring our models are deployed responsibly and have a positive impact on society. Our work spans diverse research and engineering initiatives—from system-level safeguards and model training to evaluation and red-teaming—all aimed at mitigating misuse and maintaining our high bar for safety. We lead OpenAI's commitment to developing and deploying safe Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), fostering a culture of trust, responsibility, and transparency.
Our goal is to continuously learn from deployments, distribute AI’s benefits widely, and ensure that powerful tools remain aligned with human values and safety considerations.
About the Role
The Safety Measurement Research Program Manager drives OpenAI’s strategy for safety measurement and evaluations, partnering closely with safety research, data science, and engineering to advance how we measure harm and safeguard efficacy across research and production.
You will work directly with researchers, data scientists, policy owners, and product teams who contribute to or use our measurement systems, identifying the most important problems to solve and shaping the data, dashboards, tools, and workflows we build for them. This role combines measurement expertise, product judgment, and cross-functional execution: you will engage with evaluation results and data workflows, make prioritization tradeoffs, and drive work from problem definition through rollout and iteration.
This position is based in San Francisco, CA, with relocation assistance available.
In this role, you will:
- Define strategic priorities and product roadmaps to improve safety measurement and evaluation approaches and scale our measurement platform to new use cases, products, and the needs of cross-functional teams
- Partner closely with research, data science, engineering, policy teams, and other stakeholders to craft a vision for understanding safety outcomes and prevalence across our products, and translate that vision into concrete programs of work.
- Drive the integration of cutting-edge AI safety research into OpenAI’s safety measurement and evaluation platforms, working with researchers, data scientists, and engineers to navigate technical tradeoffs, coordinate dependencies, and resolve blockers.
- Develop and continuously refine clear, actionable success criteria that effectively capture our ambitions with safety measurement and evals.
- Represent quantitative progress on safety to senior leadership.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have 6+ years of experience in research program management, technical program management, product management, or related roles, with expertise in AI safety, trust & safety, integrity, or related domains.
- Have a strong foundation in data science, statistics, economics, or a related field, and hands-on experience with measurement or evaluations.
- Enjoy working at the intersection of data science and AI safety research, translating evolving measurement needs into clear requirements, priorities, and roadmaps.
- Can independently drive complex, cross-functional programs from problem definition through rollout, building alignment and unblocking decisions in ambiguous spaces.
- Ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions, and exercise sound judgment about technical tradeoffs and the strengths and limitations of metrics and evaluations.
- Build strong partnerships across research, data science, engineering, policy, and product, and communicate complex findings clearly to technical teams and leadership.
- Are curious about AI safety and its societal impacts, learn new domains quickly, and adapt as research and priorities evolve.

About the Team
Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.
The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.
About the Role
We are seeking a senior Global Security Investigator with a technical background to lead complex, long-running security investigations involving a full spectrum of threats – whether originating from internal employees, external threat actors, or supply chain partners. This role is about seeing the full chessboard and independently driving complex, multi-month cases across cyber, physical, and human domains.
In this role you will:
- Independently conduct comprehensive security investigations from initial detection to resolution, including cases involving insiders, external actors, and supply chain and third-party risks.
- Lead proactive, data-driven threat-hunting efforts that weave together disparate signals to surface undetected insider or external threats before they escalate into incidents.
- Perform comprehensive technical analysis of complex hardware, software, and supplier supply chains to identify, enumerate, and mitigate risks.
- Partner closely with cross-functional teams, including Human Resources, Legal, Security, and IT, and external stakeholders or law enforcement when necessary.
- Collaborate with technical counterparts to enhance detections, resolve telemetry gaps, and implement new capabilities to identify security issues involving cyber, physical, and human domains.
- Collect, preserve, and analyze evidence from a variety of sources, including log data, digital forensics, subject interviews, access records, threat intelligence, and open-source intelligence (OSINT), to support investigative findings.
- Continuously improve investigative procedures and security controls based on investigations and lessons learned.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Cybersecurity, or a related field (or equivalent experience) and 8+ years of investigative experience in counterintelligence, insider risk, forensic investigations, cybersecurity, supply chain security, or related domains.
- Unimpeachable integrity, sound judgment, and the ability to handle confidential matters with discretion.
- An active US security clearance, or willingness and eligibility to obtain one.
- Deep specialization in geopolitical threat domains, with hands-on experience identifying, assessing, and mitigating adversarial risks through tailored countermeasures.
- Expert knowledge of common security tooling, including EDR, DLP, UEBA, SIEM, SOAR and other related platforms.
- Demonstrated ability to independently write complex queries, automate data workflows, and analyze structured datasets.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex findings into clear, actionable reports and explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders.
- Exceptional collaboration skills with the ability to work across diverse teams (HR, Legal, IT, etc.) to lead projects and investigations with minimal guidance.

Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models. We work across research, engineering, product, and policy to understand risks, develop and validate safeguards, and support responsible deployment.
Our work spans safeguards research and deployment, safety assessments, launch readiness, and trusted-access programs for advanced capabilities. We address risks including biological and cyber misuse and misalignment, with programs that strengthen safety across models and products.
About the Role
We’re hiring Research Program Managers across AI Safeguards and Frontier Risks Safety. You’ll lead programs that develop and improve the safeguards used across our models and products, or assess and mitigate risks associated with frontier capabilities, launches, and trusted-access programs.
You will partner with researchers, engineers, and other stakeholders to turn open safety questions into clear programs of work. You’ll shape technical roadmaps, coordinate execution, and use evidence to guide priorities and inform development and deployment decisions. We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience managing complex research programs, and a commitment to AI safety.
These roles are based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
- Shape safety programs and technical roadmaps. Partner with research and engineering leads to define goals, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria. Prioritize intake and emerging findings, resolve blockers, and balance immediate safety needs with longer-term research and platform investments.
- Drive safeguards development and deployment. Translate safety research into safeguards across models and products. Maintain an end-to-end view of safeguard coverage, effectiveness, and opportunities for improvement for one or more risk areas, and drive a roadmap that advances across launches.
- Coordinate evaluations and safety assessments. Organize capability evaluations, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including risks from autonomous and multi-agent systems. Support embedded assessments throughout model development, internal use, and deployment.
- Drive safety readiness and trusted-access programs. Coordinate safety requirements and execution across frontier model launches and deployments. Work with technical teams to define assessment scope and the evidence needed to inform safety and access decisions.
- Turn findings into improvements. Triage safeguard gaps, jailbreaks, and overflagging with accountable teams. Establish owners and escalation paths, track remediation and regression testing, and turn recurring issues into research and engineering improvements.
- Strengthen the evidence behind safety decisions. Support safety cases that connect claims to evaluations, safeguards, assumptions, and remaining uncertainty. Surface evidence gaps and unresolved risks, and communicate methods, results, limitations, and follow-up actions through assessment reports, system cards, and updates to decision-makers.
- Build programs that scale across products. Coordinate shared tooling and feedback workflows, privacy and security requirements, and safeguard user experience and quality assurance. Help teams apply safeguards consistently across product surfaces and upcoming launches.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have 5+ years of experience in technical safety work, owning technical programs, or related roles in fast-moving environments.
- Have led complex research or technical programs involving researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences.
- Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evaluations, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams.
- Can assess what evaluation results do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and the difference between model capability and real-world risk.
- Can turn ambiguous questions into clear programs, make practical tradeoffs, and adjust priorities as evidence changes.
- Have worked extensively across research, engineering, and product teams and can coordinate with policy and communications partners.

About the Team
API Multicloud partners with cloud service providers (CSPs) to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and APIs into the cloud environments where developers and enterprises already build. We own the API end to end across CSP platforms, from API integration and request routing through inference execution, capacity management, and day-to-day operations. Our mission is to make these capabilities available broadly and safely while preserving the reliability and developer experience customers expect from OpenAI.
Delivering that experience requires work across the stack: adapting API services and cloud-native integrations, bringing up model-serving environments, validating new releases, and operating the systems that connect customer requests to available capacity. We work directly with CSP engineering teams and partner closely with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems teams. Together, we turn new model capabilities and partner requirements into dependable production services, with attention to performance, operational readiness, and efficient use of compute.
Our work contributes to OpenAI’s AWS partnership https://openai.com/index/openai-on-aws/, including the launch of Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/openai-daybreak-red-and-blue-on-amazon-bedrock/ — and OpenAI’s newly announced Google Cloud partnership https://openai.com/index/openai-models-google-cloud/ will bring our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. These efforts let customers use OpenAI capabilities within the cloud infrastructure, security controls, and workflows they already rely on.
About the Role
We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead the team responsible for building and operating OpenAI’s API across major cloud service providers. You’ll lead a team of engineers focused on establishing scalable, reliable, and efficient cloud deployment platforms that bring OpenAI’s frontier models to customers across multiple cloud environments.
In this role, you'll own the technical direction, execution, and operational excellence of the API Multicloud platform. You'll guide your team through complex infrastructure challenges, including deploying model-serving environments, scaling capacity, optimizing performance and utilization, and building reusable systems that enable OpenAI to expand across CSP platforms. You'll balance long-term architectural investments with the urgency of delivering new model capabilities and partner integrations.
You'll work closely with engineering leaders across inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems, while building strong technical partnerships with CSP engineering teams. Your team will play a critical role in determining how quickly OpenAI can bring new models to market, how reliably those models operate, and how efficiently we scale our infrastructure across cloud providers.
You'll also be responsible for building and developing a high-performing engineering team, setting clear technical priorities, and fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, and operational excellence.
In this role, you will:
- Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering team responsible for building and operating OpenAI's API infrastructure across multiple cloud providers.
- Define the technical vision, strategy, and roadmap for API Multicloud, ensuring the platform is scalable, reliable, and efficient.
- Drive the architecture and execution of complex distributed systems that support API routing, model serving, and cloud infrastructure across CSP environments.
- Partner closely with inference, API, infrastructure, security, and CSP engineering teams to launch new models, expand platform capabilities, and deliver reliable production services.
- Own the reliability, performance, and operational excellence of the platform, driving improvements in capacity planning, infrastructure efficiency, and deployment processes.
- Recruit and develop exceptional engineering talent, fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and continuous improvement.
- Set clear priorities, navigate ambiguity, and drive cross-functional execution while balancing near-term business needs with long-term technical investments.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- Experience leading, building, and developing high-performing engineering teams responsible for large-scale cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, or platform engineering.
- Strong technical background in distributed systems and cloud infrastructure, with the ability to drive architectural decisions and provide technical guidance to senior engineers.
- Experience building and operating production infrastructure on major cloud platforms such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure.

About the Team
OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, our custom silicon program, the team works across silicon architecture, RTL design, verification, physical design, systems software, and infrastructure to deliver highly performant, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions.
The Silicon & Systems team brings together hardware and software engineers to co-design and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of silicon, systems, and software, tackling complex technical challenges across the full hardware development lifecycle, from early architecture and design through validation, deployment, and production.
About the Role
We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure and developer workflows that power OpenAI’s custom silicon development. You’ll work closely with engineering teams across design verification, physical design, emulation, formal verification, and systems software to develop reliable, automated, and efficient workflows that accelerate hardware development.
In this role, you'll own and improve the cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) environments, CI/CD pipelines, regression systems, and data platforms that support our silicon engineering teams. You'll translate complex hardware development requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions, reducing manual overhead, improving reliability, and enabling engineers to iterate faster.
This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role with opportunities to drive improvements across the entire hardware development lifecycle. We're looking for engineers who bring deep expertise in one or more infrastructure domains, strong software engineering fundamentals, and an interest in expanding their impact across the broader platform.
In this role, you will:
- Build developer tools and workflows: Partner with hardware engineering teams to understand their development processes, identify bottlenecks, and build tooling, services, and APIs that automate workflows and accelerate engineering productivity.
- Develop and scale regression infrastructure: Design, implement, and operate large-scale regression systems spanning job scheduling, execution, results collection, triage, and reporting, with a focus on performance, reliability, and reproducibility.
- Own CI/CD infrastructure: Build and maintain automated pipelines for infrastructure, developer tooling, and cluster configurations, enabling safe deployments, testing, and continuous improvement.
- Scale cloud and HPC environments: Design, provision, and operate cloud infrastructure and high-performance compute clusters, optimizing scheduling, capacity, reliability, and cost efficiency to support demanding silicon development workloads.
- Build data infrastructure and observability: Develop data pipelines, databases, and monitoring systems that provide visibility into regression results, infrastructure health, resource utilization, and engineering efficiency.
- Drive platform reliability and operational excellence: Troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, improve monitoring and alerting, automate recovery processes, and build systems that are resilient, maintainable, and scalable.
- Collaborate across hardware and software teams: Work directly with engineers across RTL, verification, physical design, emulation, and software to continuously improve the infrastructure supporting OpenAI's silicon development.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have strong software engineering fundamentals, with proficiency in Python or a similar programming language and experience building reliable automation, tools, or infrastructure services.
- Bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of infrastructure engineering, such as Linux/HPC environments, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD systems, storage, networking, or EDA development workflows.
- Have experience designing, deploying, and operating cloud infrastructure, preferably Azure, with familiarity in infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Bicep.
- Have strong Linux systems knowledge, including processes, filesystems, networking, permissions, performance troubleshooting, and system administration.
- Have experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, Buildkite, GitHub Actions, or similar platforms.
- Are comfortable debugging complex distributed infrastructure problems, identifying root causes, and implementing durable solutions.
- Enjoy working closely with engineering teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into scalable, practical infrastructure solutions.
- Take ownership of systems end to end, from initial design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and ongoing operational improvements.
- Bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a collaborative approach to solving ambiguous engineering challenges.
- Are curious about hardware development and excited to expand your technical expertise across infrastructure, silicon design workflows, and developer productivity.
Bonus Qualifications
- Experience supporting ASIC or semiconductor development environments, including EDA workflows, design verification, physical design, emulation, or formal verification.
- Experience operating large-scale HPC clusters or workload schedulers such as Slurm.
- Familiarity with compute farms, regression frameworks, build systems, and hardware development toolchains.
- Experience with enterprise identity and authentication systems, such as Entra ID, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA, or SSSD.
- Experience designing and operating relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL, including schema design, migrations, query optimization, and backups.
- Familiarity with distributed systems components, including message queues, caching layers, artifact storage, and backend services.
- Experience with high-performance storage systems, data movement optimization, or large-scale compute infrastructure.
- Experience managing EDA license servers, license utilization, or other shared infrastructure resources in hardware development environments.

About the Team
OpenAI's Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI's mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. If you're passionate about doing significant and unique work as a technology lawyer, this team is for you. The team comprises legal professionals from diverse fields, including technology, privacy, IP, corporate, cybersecurity, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation.
About the Role
We’re growing our IP team and seek an experienced attorney to lead OpenAI’s global trademark litigation and disputes strategy, and oversee our broader trademark and brand protection practice. You will lead complex, high-stakes trademark litigation and enforcement matters around the world, develop strategies to protect OpenAI’s brands in a rapidly evolving technological landscape, and provide practical, business-oriented advice on novel trademark and brand-related issues. This role is highly cross-functional across OpenAI, including work across our Legal, Communications, Global Affairs, Marketing, Product and Executive teams
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
- Lead global trademark litigation and disputes, including complex infringement, unfair competition, dilution, and other brand-related litigation, from initial assessment through resolution.
- Develop and execute global trademark litigation and enforcement strategies, including managing outside counsel, directing litigation strategy, assessing risk, and advising senior leadership on significant disputes.
- Lead and develop OpenAI’s trademark team, overseeing attorneys and legal professionals responsible for trademark clearance, prosecution, portfolio management, enforcement, dispute resolution, brand protection, and marketing counseling.
- Stay current on relevant laws, regulations, and industry trends, and provide updates and legal guidance to company leadership and stakeholders.
- Build scalable processes and frameworks for trademark risk assessment, enforcement prioritization, outside counsel management, and cross-functional decision-making.
- Provide clear, practical, and strategic advice to senior leadership, balancing legal risks, commercial priorities, reputational considerations, and long-term brand protection.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have 10+ years of leading complex trademark litigation and disputes, including significant responsibility for litigation strategy, case management, and resolution, including substantial experience at technology companies and law firms.
- Have personally developed and executed strategies for complex, high-stakes trademark litigation and disputes, leading matters from initial assessment through resolution, including direct engagement with opposing counsel and other key stakeholders.
- Have experience developing and executing global trademark portfolio strategies, including clearance, prosecution, enforcement, and brand protection, aligned with business priorities and growth.
- Communicate complex legal and business issues clearly, exercise sound judgment in navigating legal uncertainty, and provide practical, strategic recommendations under pressure.
- Work effectively with cross-functional teams, legal operations, outside counsel, and senior stakeholders while managing multiple urgent matters.
- Bring intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, a strong sense of ownership, and a willingness to challenge assumptions respectfully and learn from feedback.
- Have a JD and a license or qualification to practice in California.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their business. The team is made of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals that work together to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

Our Sales team has a unique mission to help customers understand the deep impact that highly capable AI models can bring to their business and users. This role is a mixture of technical understanding, vision, partnership, and value-driven strategy.
You’ll be a key driver of opportunities through the entire sales cycle, from pipeline generation to closure. You’ll work with researchers, engineers, and solution strategists to help customers evolve their industry with AI.
This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Working with partner executives and security practitioners, you’ll turn customer needs into joint opportunities, successful deployments, and repeatable offerings. This role combines executive partnership leadership with direct responsibility for growing the business in a rapidly developing market.
This is a hands-on partner sales role spanning global system integrators (GSIs), managed security service providers (MSSPs), hyperscalers, security independent software vendors (ISVs), and value-added resellers (VARs). You’ll develop partner capabilities for your assigned territory or portfolio and work alongside partner sellers and OpenAI account teams to sell joint solutions and expand customer adoption.
In this role, you will:
- Own commercial results. Grow revenue through partner relationships. Build qualified pipeline, progress opportunities, and support sustained customer use and expansion. Maintain accurate opportunity records and a disciplined forecast.
- Build partner plans and practices. Work with partner executives and technical teams to turn customer demand into joint business plans and commercially viable cybersecurity offerings. Help partners establish the service economics, practitioner capacity, and delivery quality needed to build a repeatable business.
