- Improve execution with evidence. Use what you learn from customer evaluations and deployments to improve offerings. Bring recurring needs and practical lessons to OpenAI’s product, technical, and go-to-market teams.
You’ll own the partner business plan and commercial execution for your assigned territory or portfolio, working closely with OpenAI account teams, alliance leaders, and technical specialists. Together, you’ll develop customer opportunities, establish realistic delivery plans, and help partners support successful adoption.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- A record of delivering revenue through enterprise partner sales, alliances, or business development in cybersecurity, cloud, or AI, including personally progressing complex customer opportunities.
- Strong partner business acumen and experience building repeatable offerings. You understand how services firms, managed security providers, cloud providers, security software companies, and resellers invest, make money, and mobilize their sellers and practitioners.
- Credibility with enterprise security buyers and practitioners. You can explain how AI capabilities fit into security workflows, recognize the importance of tools, context, and permissions, and involve technical specialists to validate customer commitments.
- Experience helping enterprise customers adopt a new product while its market was still forming.
- The ability to earn trust with partner executives and champions while working effectively with account teams, alliance leaders, technical teams, Product, and Marketing.

- Deeper familiarity with how a model and its harness work together, including how the surrounding software supplies tools and context and enforces permissions.

- Active partner champions and commercially viable practices and offerings that generate repeatable customer opportunities.
- Customer deployments that progress to sustained use, expansion, and demonstrable security outcomes.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The AI Deployment Manager (ADM) team enables organizations to turn OpenAI products into real, sustained impact through world-class enablement and training execution.
Our mission is to help customers successfully adopt and operationalize AI across their organizations. We partner with enterprises to translate the potential of OpenAI’s technology into durable capability—through structured training, technical enablement, and scalable deployment programs.
By helping customers move from experimentation to production, the ADM team accelerates time-to-value, deepens meaningful adoption, and helps make OpenAI indispensable to how organizations work.
About the Role
The AI Deployment Manager, Builder role is a specialist post-sales technical enablement role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. You will design and deliver technical learning experiences covering OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, evaluations, and related platform capabilities. You will work with engineers, AI and platform teams, administrators, security stakeholders, product leaders, and executive sponsors.
This role blends deep technical fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live trainings, workshops, and adoption interventions for audiences ranging from hands-on builders to executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to use them effectively in real-world contexts.
Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, helping customers progress toward production use, and turning lessons from individual engagements into resources and practices that benefit many customers.
This role is based in San Francisco or New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
- Own the technical enablement of OpenAI products, including OpenAI APIs, Codex, Agents, Evaluations and other platform capabilities, helping define effective enablement patterns that support adoption across customer segments
- Lead customer training and enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.
- Design and deliver high-impact training engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.
- Drive customer activation, sustained usage, and measurable business value through structured enablement and deployment programs designed for durable adoption at scale
- Partner closely with Sales, Solutions Architecture, and Product teams to define an effective enablement plan tailored to each customer’s use case, goals, and technical needs.
- Partner closely with Sales, Solution Architects, Delivery Leads to drive adoption across our core product suite.
- Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.
- Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.
- Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.
YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have 4+ years of experience in customer-facing or instructional roles, engaging C-level and senior technical audiences in complex enterprise environments.
- Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when conveying the value of technical concepts clearly to senior and executive-level audiences.
- Strong technical depth across software engineering, the software development lifecycle, and APIs, with a practical understanding of how AI systems are built, evaluated, and operated in production, including RAG, evaluation strategies, agentic systems and key tradeoffs.
- Proven experience leading structured technical trainings, such as API bootcamps, workshops, or enablement sessions, with the ability to design learning journeys, handle live questions, and reason through problems in real time.

About the Team
OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.
About the Role
We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.
You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties—often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.
We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.
This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will be:
- Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.
- Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.
- Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.
- Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.
- Partnering with Privacy, Product, Regulatory, and other counsel to assess notification and reporting obligations, advise on timely customer and user communications, and coordinate third-party outreach and incident-related information sharing with industry peers and government partners.
- Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.
- Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.
- Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.
- 5+ years of relevant experience.
- Relevant legal experience managing cybersecurity or privacy incident responses or comparable complex technology investigations at a technology company, law firm, or government agency, including work with technical teams, other counsel, and communications partners.
- The ability to translate technical findings into practical legal advice, with a working understanding of technical information.
- Sound judgment under time pressure, clear communication of uncertainty, and an understanding of when to act, seek specialist advice, or escalate.
- Clear, concise writing and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned through changing facts and competing priorities.
- Ownership of details and follow-through, paired with collaborative work with colleagues who bring different expertise.
- A strong interest in the novel challenges of AI safety and a willingness to help develop new approaches. Direct AI incident experience is helpful; strong transferable incident response skills are welcome.
- Availability to participate in time-sensitive incident response, including occasional work outside normal business hours.

About the Team
Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.
We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.
That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.
Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.
We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.
In this role, you will:
- Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.
- Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.
- Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.
- Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.
- Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.
- Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.
- Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.
- Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.
- Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.
Nice to Have
- Experience with payments, subscriptions, pricing, billing, or other systems that manage customer purchases and revenue.
- Experience with product catalogs, packaging and bundles, workspace management, entitlements, or usage metering.
- Experience building financial or transaction systems at scale, checking that records match across systems, or supporting compliance and audits.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Strategic Finance Data Science team helps OpenAI understand business performance and make informed decisions about growth, revenue, and resource allocation. We partner with Strategic Finance, Data Engineering, and business teams to build trusted metrics, explain what is changing, and support forecasting, planning, pricing, and investment decisions.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for a Data Scientist, Analytics Enablement to turn complex financial and business questions into reliable data products, clear analyses, and actionable recommendations. You will work across the analytical workflow: define the question, establish trustworthy metrics and datasets, investigate the drivers, and help partners act on the findings.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will combine the technical depth of analytics engineering with strong analytical judgment and close partnership with Strategic Finance. Your work will serve both executive reviews and the teams making day-to-day business decisions.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL
- Define and maintain trusted metrics and analytical datasets for revenue, usage, customer performance, compute consumption, and margin, with clear definitions and appropriate product, customer, and cohort detail.
- Build automated dashboards and recurring reporting that help Finance leaders and operating teams understand performance, spot changes, and prioritize investigation.
- Explain movements in business results and variances against expectations by examining underlying drivers, validating data quality, and distinguishing evidence from assumptions.
- Translate ambiguous questions about growth, retention, monetization, pricing, and resource efficiency into structured analyses and practical recommendations.
- Partner with forecasting specialists and Finance to provide reliable inputs, driver analyses, and scenario assumptions for forecasts and long-range plans.
- Work with Data Engineering to improve the quality and usability of underlying data, and develop reusable analytical models and workflows that reduce manual effort.
- Communicate findings clearly, align stakeholders on trade-offs, and follow through to understand whether the analysis or data product improved the decision.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU
- Have strong SQL and analytical data-modeling skills, and experience turning large, complex datasets into reliable analyses and reusable data products.
- Can reason carefully about metrics, cohorts, denominators, measurement changes, and uncertainty, and investigate whether an unexpected result reflects the business or the data.
- Have built dashboards or recurring reporting used by business partners, and can explain the decisions they enabled.
- Bring sound business judgment and can independently scope an ambiguous problem, prioritize the work, and deliver an end-to-end solution.
- Communicate technical findings clearly and work effectively with Finance, data scientists, engineers, and other business partners.
- Can use Python or a comparable analytical tool to investigate data and automate repetitive work.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation models. We operate a large, modern GPU fleet and provide a unified platform for other OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads.
We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You will join the Compute Infrastructure TPM team as a Technical Program Manager for Capacity Analytics & Tooling. You will serve as the product manager for our supply and demand planning tools, owning the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of the systems teams use to forecast demand, understand supply, and plan allocations. Your users will include Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside partners across Finance, Accounting, Leadership, Engineering, and Research.
This role combines product management, technical program leadership, data engineering, and applied data science. You will partner with engineering and data teams to build reliable data foundations, improve forecasting and scenario planning, and scale our tools and success metrics across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources. You will help teams make informed capacity decisions across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure providers.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Own the product strategy and roadmap for supply and demand planning tools. Understand user needs, set priorities, define success measures, and guide delivery from initial requirements through adoption and ongoing improvement.
- Build useful planning workflows. Translate complex processes into tools for demand intake, forecasting, supply tracking, scenario analysis, and allocation planning. Help teams understand what infrastructure they need, when it will be available, and which gaps require action.
- Scale the data infrastructure behind capacity planning. Partner with engineering on ingestion, transformation, storage, and delivery of planning data. Guide technical tradeoffs as the number of resources, providers, data sources, and users grows.
- Make planning data consistent and trustworthy. Establish shared data models and definitions for supply, demand, allocations, utilization, and cost. Drive data cleaning, validation, reconciliation, and traceability so users can understand and trust planning outputs.
- Advance forecasting and analytical capabilities. Work with engineering and data partners to connect product and research plans to infrastructure demand. Make assumptions, uncertainty, forecast accuracy, and capacity constraints visible to decision makers.
- Define and scale meaningful success metrics. Measure data quality, forecast performance, planning speed, and tool adoption. Establish consistent ways to track capacity availability, utilization, and efficiency across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources.
- Support planning across multiple cloud providers. Build capabilities that account for differences in resource types, regions, availability, commercial commitments, and deployment constraints across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other providers.
- Lead delivery across data, infrastructure, and planning teams. Manage dependencies, technical tradeoffs, migrations, risks, and releases. Keep teams aligned on priorities and the decisions needed to move work forward.
- Drive adoption and reduce manual planning work. Develop simple workflows, documentation, training, and feedback mechanisms. Identify recurring reconciliation and reporting work that can be improved through better data and automation.
- Make capacity tradeoffs clear to leadership and partner teams. Provide useful views of gaps between supply and demand, allocation options, and their financial and operational consequences. Partner with Finance and Accounting to align planning data with budgeting and reporting needs.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have 5+ years of experience leading technical programs or products in data platforms, infrastructure, capacity planning, or a related field, with a record of delivering systems that teams rely on.
- Have owned an internal product or platform roadmap and translated complex operational needs into requirements, priorities, and releases that users adopt.
- Have direct experience with capacity planning, including demand forecasting, supply planning, allocations, and resource constraints. You understand how utilization, performance, availability, and cost affect planning decisions.
- Understand modern data infrastructure, including ingestion, transformation, batch and streaming processing, and analytical storage. You have worked with technologies such as Fivetran, dbt, Spark, Kafka, or comparable systems and can discuss their architectural tradeoffs.
- Have practical experience with data modeling, data cleaning, validation, and reconciliation. You can use SQL and Python or similar tools to investigate discrepancies, validate assumptions, and prototype analyses.
- Have applied quantitative methods to forecasting, scenario analysis, or optimization. You can assess model assumptions and uncertainty, evaluate forecast performance, and explain the limitations of an analysis.
- Understand the capacity, performance, and cost characteristics of compute, storage, networking, and accelerators. You have experience working across multiple cloud environments and can account for differences between providers.
- Can lead complex programs with many technical dependencies and align teams with different priorities. You communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to engineers, researchers, finance partners, and leaders.
- Are resourceful in ambiguous environments, exercise sound product judgment, and build simple, scalable ways to solve complex planning problems.
- Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI.

About the Team
The Consulting team is part of OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. Our goal is to help consulting teams do better work for their clients. We work side by side with design partners to understand how their teams operate, then use what we learn to build for consultants everywhere.
Today, we’re bringing OpenAI’s models and products together to accelerate the core work of consulting, from investigating a client’s question to delivering advice they can act on. We’re starting by removing the barriers that keep consultants from using AI in their day-to-day work. We’ll draw on the full range of OpenAI’s capabilities, from ChatGPT Work to newer tools such as Dots and Spaces.
Longer term, we want to help firms develop AI-native ways of working. A team could design an engagement around questions it can now afford to explore, test several strategies with its client, and change course as it learns what works. We’re moving quickly, working across OpenAI’s research, product, and engineering teams to turn what we learn with design partners into products consultants everywhere can use.
About the Role
We’re looking for a full-stack software engineer to build first-party OpenAI products for consulting. You’ll own features end to end, from the frontend interfaces consultants use to the backend services and integrations that power them.
You’ll work closely with our consulting design partners and with colleagues across product, design, research, and engineering at OpenAI. Together, you’ll turn what you learn from individual engagement teams into products we can distribute broadly. Success will ultimately be defined by adoption and the value generated for consulting firms.
In this role, you will:
- Work directly with our design partners. Sit with consultants and engagement leaders, observe how they work, and identify problems worth solving across firms.
- Design and prototype experiences that help consultants do an important part of their job better from day one.
- Build across the stack, from the user interface to the services and APIs that connect OpenAI’s models with the tools consultants use.
- Build for firms with different methods and working environments while protecting the confidential information clients entrust to them.
- Evaluate what you build with design partners and researchers. Use real assignments to see where it improves the work and what still needs to change.
- Ship the product to consulting teams broadly and own its rollout and reliability. Use feedback and production data to guide improvements after launch.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have shipped and operated a substantial product, with hands-on ownership across frontend and backend systems.
- Have strong product and interface instincts, especially when people need to understand, question, or correct what software produces.
- Enjoy working directly with users and can tell when one customer’s request points to a problem many people share.
- Can turn an unfamiliar workflow into a working prototype, then make the technical choices it takes to support many teams.
- Make thoughtful tradeoffs about quality, speed, and reliability and can explain those choices to colleagues across disciplines.
Nice to Have
- Firsthand consulting experience combined with hands-on experience building and shipping software.
- Building software for research, analysis, collaboration, or other complex professional work.
- Developing AI applications and evaluating their usefulness with expert users.
- Designing enterprise products that handle sensitive information or fit into different organizations’ ways of working.
- Taking a product from its first few users to broad adoption as a founder or early engineer.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Research Compute Services builds the systems that help researchers use OpenAI’s compute fleet effectively. We partner with Research and Compute Infrastructure to support workloads across the compute stack, including pretraining, synthetic data generation, sampling, research inference, and reinforcement learning.
Our work connects changing research needs with capacity planning, allocation, and scheduling. We build tools and services that help researchers express their compute needs, access the right resources, and run their workloads effectively. As the fleet and our research ambitions grow, we continually improve how compute is planned, allocated, and used.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, partnering closely with the Research Compute Services team. Your primary responsibility will be to build and own the tools, data, and platform that turn Research plans and workload signals into concrete compute demand and manage allocations across the fleet.
This is a hands-on technical role. You will build alongside researchers and engineers, working directly with code and data to prototype solutions, automate workflows, and deliver tools that teams use every day. You will combine technical judgment and program leadership to connect capacity planning with the deployment, scheduling, and optimization systems that make allocated compute usable.
You will work across a broad range of Research workloads, understanding their different requirements and ensuring those needs shape the platform. Success means researchers can express their needs, understand their allocations, and use compute effectively as priorities and workloads change.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Build with Research. Work directly with researchers across pretraining, research inference, and other workloads. Treat these communities as core users, and translate their needs into improvements across compute services, tooling, and scheduling.
- Own Research demand and allocation systems. Own the roadmap and delivery of the tools, data, and platform used to capture demand, support allocation decisions, and manage allocations. Carry this work from requirements and design through adoption and ongoing improvement.
- Turn research plans into actionable demand. Develop systems that translate evolving plans and workload requirements into concrete capacity needs, including resource requirements, timing, and constraints.
- Connect capacity supply and demand. Partner with Capacity Planning, Research, and infrastructure teams to reconcile demand with available supply. Build the tools and workflows needed to evaluate scenarios, manage changes, and make allocation tradeoffs visible to decision makers.
- Build reliable data and useful tools. Create data models, views, and automation that show what researchers need, what capacity is available, what has been allocated, and how it is being used. Improve self-service workflows for requesting and managing compute.
- Connect allocations to workload execution. Partner with engineers working on Kubernetes deployments and scheduling systems so allocation plans reflect workload constraints and translate into resources that researchers can use.
- Improve allocation and scheduling efficiency. Work with engineers to evaluate optimization approaches, including solvers operating at fleet and local scheduling levels. Help define constraints and objectives, assess tradeoffs, and measure improvements in fleet utilization.
- Find and address systemic gaps. Use workload and fleet data to identify bottlenecks, unused capacity, and recurring manual work. Build durable improvements to the tools and systems behind those problems.
- Lead technical delivery across teams. Own plans, dependencies, and decisions across Research, Research Compute Services, Capacity Planning, and infrastructure engineering. Keep teams aligned on what needs to be built, how it will be adopted, and who will operate it.
- Make progress and tradeoffs clear. Give working teams and leadership a clear view of demand, allocation constraints, delivery progress, and decisions that need attention.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have a strong engineering foundation, developed through relevant education or demonstrated technical experience.
- Have led and delivered complex technical programs involving large-scale compute, distributed systems, infrastructure platforms, or research environments.
- Have practical experience with capacity planning, including supply and demand management, compute allocations, and the tools and data that support those decisions.
- Have personally built or materially contributed to tools, data systems, or automation used by engineering or research teams. You are comfortable working directly with code and operational data.
- Are familiar with Kubernetes deployments and scheduling systems, and understand how resource constraints and placement decisions affect workload execution.
- Understand optimization solvers and can reason about their use in fleet-wide allocation and local scheduling. You can evaluate constraints, objectives, and tradeoffs without losing sight of researcher needs.
- Can work closely with researchers to understand evolving requirements and translate them into systems that are practical to build and useful in daily work.
- Can take ownership of ambiguous technical problems, establish a clear path forward, and bring complex work through delivery and adoption.
- Communicate technical decisions, constraints, and priorities clearly across engineering, Research, and leadership.
- Are resourceful, comfortable with changing priorities, and motivated by improving both researcher productivity and compute efficiency.
- Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large compute clusters that support OpenAI’s research, ChatGPT, and the API. Our work spans GPUs, CPUs, storage, networking, and cloud infrastructure, bringing these systems together so teams can train and serve models at scale.
We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You will own CPU capacity planning and management across Research and Compute. Working with infrastructure owners, you will lead integrated planning for CPU, storage, and network capacity across OpenAI’s global fleet. You will connect workload demand and GPU deployment plans with the foundational resources required to support pretraining, research, and application infrastructure at scale.
You will work closely with workload owners, infrastructure engineering, network deployment teams, Finance, and cloud providers to turn forecasts into supply and allocation plans. You will understand workload architecture, guide decisions when capacity is constrained, and drive opportunities to improve utilization and reduce waste. Your work will span planning over multiple years and ongoing capacity management across regions and providers, including AWS, GCP, Azure, and OCI.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:
- Lead CPU demand planning across Research, Compute, and application infrastructure, including foundational services, data acquisition, container platforms, robotics, and services supporting GPU clusters. Maintain forecasts that capture workload growth, regional and hardware requirements, timing, and acceptable alternatives.
- Translate workload growth and GPU fleet plans into integrated CPU, storage, and network requirements. Partner with engineering to determine the capacity, throughput, bandwidth, connectivity, and placement needed to support pretraining and applications at scale.
- Reconcile current and incoming supply with demand, model constrained scenarios, and drive allocation and prioritization decisions. Lead CPU allocation planning and fulfillment, including quota transfers, rebalancing, and reclaims.
- Partner with network engineering and deployment teams to translate regional demand into bandwidth and connectivity plans, ordering inputs, and delivery milestones. Coordinate CPU and network allocations as capacity is deployed across the fleet.
- Understand workload architecture and performance requirements well enough to challenge assumptions and influence technical decisions. Help teams evaluate resource sizing, regional placement, data movement, storage choices, and acceptable alternatives when supply is constrained.
- Drive fleet efficiency programs that reclaim unused capacity, rightsize workloads, modernize infrastructure, and improve placement or resource sharing. Measure the capacity released and cost improvements while preserving workload performance and reliability.
- Scale integrated capacity planning across CPU, storage, and network in partnership with resource owners. Improve demand intake, forecasts, scenario models, inventory and allocation records, and the tools that automate recurring workflows.
- Partner with cloud providers, Finance, Procurement, and engineering to shape capacity orders, commitments, and renewal decisions. Evaluate regional availability, delivery lead times, cost, and technical fit, and drive resolution of supply gaps.
- Align capacity plans with cluster and application deployment milestones. Work across infrastructure owners to ensure CPU, storage, and network dependencies are ready when workloads need them, and resolve gaps that would delay usable capacity.
- Give teams and leadership a clear view of demand, supply, allocation tradeoffs, forecast changes, and risks. Turn ambiguous or competing needs into decisions, accountable owners, and executable plans.
YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Have 5+ years of experience in technical program management, capacity planning, capacity engineering, or infrastructure management, with ownership of complex programs at scale.
- Have directly managed demand forecasting, supply planning, allocations, and capacity operations for CPU or cloud compute infrastructure. You understand how forecasts, inventory, quotas, delivery schedules, and utilization inform capacity decisions.
- Bring technical depth in one or more infrastructure domains and can reason across the dependencies among CPUs, GPUs, storage, and networks.
- Understand how workload architecture drives CPU and memory needs, storage capacity and throughput, network bandwidth and latency, and regional placement. You can use that knowledge to influence engineering decisions.
- Have worked across multiple cloud providers and understand how provider capabilities, quotas, regional constraints, and commercial commitments affect capacity plans.
- Have built or improved capacity planning tools, data models, or automation. You are comfortable working directly with data to validate assumptions, model scenarios, and measure outcomes.
- Have delivered measurable improvements in infrastructure utilization or cost through reclaims, rightsizing, modernization, workload placement, or other efficiency programs.
- Can lead decisions across engineering, research, product, Finance, and external providers, balancing technical requirements, delivery risk, and cost. You communicate clearly with both working teams and leadership.
- Are resourceful in ambiguous environments, take ownership of outcomes, and build simple processes that continue to work as the fleet grows.
- Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI.

About the Team
Models are becoming increasingly capable—moving from tools that assist humans to agents that can plan, execute, and adapt in the real world. Mitigating the frontier risks resulting from these capabilities is paramount to OpenAI’s ability to continue deploying models safely.
The Preparedness team is dedicated to addressing these critical risks. Our work includes:
1. Measurement. Monitoring and predicting the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems.
2. Mitigation. Keeping misalignment safeguards, alignment tools, and on track to adequately address extreme threats that might arise in the future.
3. Coordination. Setting mitigation targets by maintaining OpenAI’s preparedness framework https://openai.com/index/updating-our-preparedness-framework/, and partnering with other staff to achieve these targets.
This is urgent, fast-paced work that has far-reaching implications for the company and for society.
About the Role
We’re looking for a very senior, independent Software Engineer to lead the technical work behind cyber safeguard infrastructure in Preparedness. You’ll bring production-grade engineering discipline to systems that support everything from cyber evaluations and safeguard research internally to enabling the safe deployment of capabilities externally, while working closely with researchers and security partners. The right person can move comfortably from ambiguous research needs to robust, operable systems—and can drive the work across organizational boundaries with clear communication.
In this role, you’ll:
- Drive the technical direction and hands-on execution for cyber safeguard infrastructure.
- Establish production-quality reliability, observability, on-call, and SLA/SLO practices.
- Partner with teams across the company - security, research, policy and product - to translate evolving needs into durable platforms.
- Lead cross-functional technical work, create alignment, and unblock collaborators.
- Build reliable systems that support cyber evaluations and research workflows.
- Improve the scalability, usability, and operational safety of cyber safeguards.
- Mentor teammates and raise the engineering bar while remaining deeply hands-on.
You might thrive in this role if you have:
- Extensive experience owning large-scale production systems, including reliability, on-call, incident response, SLAs/SLOs, and operational excellence.
- Senior/staff-level technical leadership with a track record of driving ambiguous, cross-functional work, especially in cybersecurity.
- Strong hands-on software engineering and systems-design skills; you can go deep in the code and architecture, including systems where you are unfamiliar and quickly gain context to make meaningful changes while following existing patterns.
- Ability to collaborate closely with researchers and independently turn evolving research needs into robust infrastructure.
- Experience thinking and communicating about cyber capability, misuse risk, access patterns, safeguards, and deployment tradeoffs in high-stakes environments.
- Experience at a security company, supporting cyber evaluations, or building security/reliability infrastructure is a plus.
- Experience moving from strong engineering into research support is a plus; former engineering managers are welcome if they remain deeply technical and hands-on.

About the team
OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with banks, asset managers, insurers, and private capital firms to deploy production-grade AI systems in high-stakes financial environments. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, embedding deeply with customers to translate frontier model capabilities into reliable, auditable systems that create measurable business impact. Our work turns early deployments into repeatable solution patterns, operating standards, and evaluation practices that scale across regulated financial institutions.
About the role
We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to lead end-to-end deployments of OpenAI’s models inside financial services organizations where correctness, latency, explainability, and control matter. You will work with customers who are experts in investment banking, trading, risk, compliance, underwriting, research, operations, or investment decision-making, translating complex workflows, data constraints, and regulatory requirements into production systems.
You will measure success through production adoption, workflow efficiency, risk reduction, revenue impact, and evaluation-driven feedback loops that inform product, model, and GTM strategy. You’ll work closely with Product, Research, GTM, Security, Legal, and GRC to deliver systems that meet enterprise standards for governance, auditability, and operational resilience.
You will also play a central role in shaping OpenAI’s Financial Services offering — identifying high-value use cases, defining solution patterns, and building the first repeatable deployments that scale across institutions. Learn more about some of our work with financial institutions https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-financial-services/.
This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% may be required.
In this role, you will:
- Design and ship production AI systems around models, owning integrations, data flows, reliability, observability, and on-call readiness across financial workflows.
- Lead discovery and scoping from pre-sales through post-production, translating ambiguous business problems into hypothesis-driven problem framing, system requirements, and delivery plans with measurable outcomes.
- Define and enforce launch criteria for regulated financial environments, including controls, audit artifacts, evaluation benchmarks, and acceptance thresholds tied to risk and performance.
- Build in sensitive data environments where access controls, data lineage, explainability, and failure modes shape architecture and operating procedures.
- Run evaluation loops that measure model and system quality against workflow-specific financial benchmarks (e.g., accuracy, latency, coverage, false positives) and use results to drive iteration.
- Own delivery state across multiple workstreams, making trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality to protect production outcomes.
- Distill deployment learnings into hardened primitives, reference architectures, playbooks, and tooling that scale across financial institutions.
- Surface field feedback that informs model behavior, product capabilities, and platform gaps in real-world financial use cases.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Bring 5+ years of software engineering, ML engineering, or technical deployment experience with customer-facing ownership in financial services or adjacent regulated industries.
- Have owned complex AI or data-driven systems end-to-end, from scoping through production adoption, in environments where errors carry real financial or regulatory consequences.
- Have experience with financial workflows such as research, trading, risk, compliance, underwriting, operations, or investment processes, and understand how incentives and controls shape adoption.
- Write and review production-grade code across backend and frontend systems using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks.
- Have deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behavior, evaluation, and guardrails affect user trust and business outcomes.
- Communicate clearly across engineering, product, risk, compliance, and executive stakeholders, translating technical trade-offs into decision quality and risk posture.
- Apply systems thinking with high execution standards, turning incidents, escalations, and failures into improved operating standards and repeatable deployment patterns.
- Stay calm and decisive when delivery is urgent, ambiguous, and high-stakes.

About the Team
The Agent Platform team at OpenAI builds the production systems that bring useful AI agents to users around the world. We provide the platform that enables agents to execute code, use tools, and interact with software reliably and securely at scale.
We work closely with product, research, and infrastructure teams to turn new agent capabilities into dependable product experiences. Our work spans the execution environments, APIs, and integrations that support agentic products such as Codex and tool use in ChatGPT.
We focus on how agents run in production: making it easy to launch new capabilities, supporting growing demand, and improving the performance and reliability of the systems behind user experiences.
Some of the hardest problems in making agents useful emerge when they meet real-world workloads. We build the platform that helps agents handle those workloads safely, recover when things go wrong, and deliver consistent results.
About the Role
As a Software Engineer on the Agent Platform team, you will build and scale the services that power agentic products at OpenAI. You’ll work closely with product engineers, researchers, and infrastructure engineers to bring new capabilities from early prototypes to production.
Your work will include designing APIs and services, improving agent execution and orchestration, and building the integrations needed to support increasingly capable agents. You’ll help launch new experiences while strengthening the reliability, observability, and efficiency of the platform underneath them.
We’re looking for engineers with experience building large-scale backend systems or infrastructure who enjoy working close to products and users. You should be comfortable moving quickly through ambiguous problems while making thoughtful decisions about security, performance, and long-term maintainability.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
- Build and operate production services that enable agents to execute code, use tools, and interact with external systems.
- Design APIs and platform abstractions that make it easier for product teams to build and launch agentic experiences.
- Develop orchestration systems that manage agent execution, state, resource allocation, retries, and recovery.
- Improve platform reliability, latency, and efficiency through performance optimization, observability, and capacity planning.
- Partner with product, research, security, and infrastructure teams to bring new agent capabilities into production.
- Own systems through their full lifecycle, from design and implementation to rollout, monitoring, and ongoing operation.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- Have experience building and operating large-scale backend services, distributed systems, or cloud infrastructure.
- Enjoy building shared platforms and APIs that help other engineers move faster.
- Can take an early prototype, turn it into a reliable service, and evolve it as usage grows.
- Have a strong understanding of system performance, concurrency, failure modes, and resource management.
- Care about how infrastructure decisions affect the user experience, including responsiveness, reliability, and predictable behavior.
- Are comfortable working across service boundaries and collaborating with teams to solve problems from end to end.
- Have experience with cloud platforms, containers, orchestration systems, or infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform.
- Are interested in secure execution environments, sandboxing, and the challenges of running agent workloads in production.

About the team
OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems.
About the role
You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions.
You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.
You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.
This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.
In this role you will:
- Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria.
- Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review.
- Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates.
- Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence.
- Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt.
You might thrive in this role if you:
- 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software.
- Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering.
- Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows.
- Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security.
- Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes.

About the role
You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.
You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.
